title: $\unicode{x1F493}$Heartian: Physiology-Aware Relightable Gaussian Head Avatar
comment: 4 pages of manuscript and 2 pages of supplementary material; SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Technical Communications
summary: Gaussian head avatars typically model intrinsic facial appearance as temporally static, omitting subtle cardiac-induced skin-color variation. We propose $\unicode{x1F493}$Heartian, a physiology-aware modulation framework that learns cardiac-cycle-dependent per-frame albedo modulation of facial skin-region Gaussians within a relightable head avatar to encode remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) signals. Using synchronized contact PPG supervision, $\unicode{x1F493}$Heartian models the prescribed cardiac waveform as the sum of two Gaussian functions and learns per-frame spatial residuals via a lightweight MLP. Across 152 stationary recordings from UBFC-rPPG, PURE, and MMPD, attribute-space recovery of the supplied signal achieves a pooled recording-level heart-rate MAE of 0.29 bpm and MAPE of 0.38%. The signals remain detectable after rendering by benchmark rPPG methods, with the best tested configuration - a motion-augmented TS-CAN decoder pretrained on UBFC-rPPG - recovering heart rate from the rendered MMPD avatars at 0.97 bpm MAE and 1.21% MAPE. Meanwhile, $\unicode{x1F493}$Heartian maintains reconstruction quality comparable to the baseline, with negligible average PSNR degradation of 0.005 dB. Overall, our work embeds recoverable rPPG signals as controllable material attributes to subject-specific Gaussian head avatars while retaining the reconstruction quality.

AI.tldr: Heartian is a physiology-aware modulation framework that embeds remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) signals into Gaussian head avatars by learning cardiac-cycle-dependent per-frame albedo modulation of facial skin regions, enabling recoverable heart rate signals while maintaining reconstruction quality.
AI.motivation: Current Gaussian head avatars model facial appearance as temporally static, omitting subtle cardiac-induced skin-color variations. This paper aims to embed recoverable rPPG signals as controllable material attributes into subject-specific Gaussian head avatars while retaining reconstruction quality.
AI.method: The proposed Heartian framework uses synchronized contact PPG supervision to model the prescribed cardiac waveform as the sum of two Gaussian functions, then learns per-frame spatial residuals via a lightweight MLP to modulate the albedo of facial skin-region Gaussians within a relightable head avatar.
AI.result: Across 152 stationary recordings from UBFC-rPPG, PURE, and MMPD datasets, the method achieves 0.29 bpm heart-rate MAE and 0.38% MAPE. After rendering, a motion-augmented TS-CAN decoder recovers heart rate at 0.97 bpm MAE and 1.21% MAPE, with negligible PSNR degradation of only 0.005 dB.
AI.conclusion: Heartian successfully embeds recoverable rPPG signals into Gaussian head avatars while maintaining comparable reconstruction quality, demonstrating the feasibility of encoding physiological signals as controllable material attributes in 3D avatar systems.

title: Token Clustering and Semantic Sequence Mamba for Hyperspectral Image Classification
summary: Although hyperspectral images (HSIs) provide rich spectral-spatial information, accurate pixel-level classification remains challenging because of spectral-spatial heterogeneity and complex spatial structures. Existing vision state space models (Mamba) typically construct sequences according to predefined spatial neighborhoods, without explicitly accounting for semantic similarity or spatial non-stationarity. To address this limitation, we propose Token Clustering and Semantic Sequence Mamba (STMamba), which organizes sparse tokens into semantically coherent sequences for hyperspectral image classification with the following features. First, at the macro level, a hierarchical encoder decoder progressively selects semantic tokens with the Token Clustering Module (TCM) and restores dense features using a parameter-free Cross-scale Neighborhood Attention (CNA) Upsampler. Second, at the micro level, TCM first identifies representative cluster centers through density-aware clustering and estimates soft memberships based on feature similarity. A quadtree-based dynamic selection strategy then retains sparse and spatially distributed tokens from each semantic cluster, forming coherent semantic-token sequences while reducing redundant pixel-wise representations. Third, parallel Spatial and Spectral Semantic-wise Sequencing Mamba (SWSM) modules capture complementary long-range spatial and spectral dependencies within homogeneous semantic token sequences while suppressing irrelevant interactions across heterogeneous regions. Experimental results on three large-scale benchmark datasets demonstrate that STMamba outperforms the SOTA methods with respect to quantitative and qualitative results.

AI.tldr: STMamba is a novel vision state space model for hyperspectral image classification that organizes sparse tokens into semantically coherent sequences using token clustering and semantic sequencing, addressing limitations of predefined spatial neighborhoods in existing Mamba models.
AI.motivation: Existing vision state space models (Mamba) construct sequences according to predefined spatial neighborhoods without explicitly accounting for semantic similarity or spatial non-stationarity, which limits accurate pixel-level classification of hyperspectral images due to spectral-spatial heterogeneity and complex spatial structures.
AI.method: The proposed STMamba has three key components: (1) A hierarchical encoder-decoder with Token Clustering Module (TCM) for progressive semantic token selection and a parameter-free Cross-scale Neighborhood Attention (CNA) Upsampler for dense feature restoration; (2) At micro level, TCM identifies representative cluster centers through density-aware clustering, estimates soft memberships based on feature similarity, and uses a quadtree-based dynamic selection strategy to retain sparse, spatially distributed tokens from each semantic cluster, forming coherent semantic-token sequences while reducing redundant pixel-wise representations; (3) Parallel Spatial and Spectral Semantic-wise Sequencing Mamba (SWSM) modules capture complementary long-range spatial and spectral dependencies within homogeneous semantic token sequences while suppressing irrelevant interactions across heterogeneous regions.
AI.result: Experimental results on three large-scale benchmark datasets demonstrate that STMamba outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative and qualitative metrics.
AI.conclusion: STMamba effectively addresses the semantic similarity and spatial non-stationarity issues in hyperspectral image classification by organizing tokens into semantically coherent sequences, achieving superior performance over existing methods.

title: M-plicits: Neural Implicit Surfaces via Nested Multiscale Residuals
summary: Encoding input coordinates with sinusoidal functions into multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) has proven effective for implicit neural representations (INRs) of surfaces defined as zero-level sets. However, existing methods often struggle to balance training efficiency, rendering speed, and noise robustness: single-MLP approaches are expensive at inference, grid-based representations are fast but can limit surface smoothness and overfit input noise, and previous multiscale approaches frequently capture noise and produce artifacts due to hard spectral truncation. To address these limitations, we propose M-plicits, a multiscale framework that models surfaces as a residual sum of MLPs trained via a sequence of nested neighborhoods. Unlike existing residual approaches that rely on standard domain-wide sampling and require costly mesh extraction for visualization, our method strictly localizes supervision to narrow bands around the previous zero-level sets. This nested design naturally provides robustness against noisy input data: the coarse network acts as a low-pass filter that establishes a clean geometric prior, while subsequent residuals progressively refine the geometry without fitting to high-frequency artifacts. We further introduce a multiscale sphere-tracing algorithm and a GEMM-based analytical normal computation that bypasses auto-differentiation entirely, yielding high-fidelity real-time rendering. On Stanford and Thingi32, M-plicits achieves the best mean Chamfer distance in the coarse configuration and the best median Chamfer distance and IoU in the fine configuration, with substantially better noise robustness than iNGP, BACON, and IDF, while using an order of magnitude fewer parameters than grid-based baselines. Code, models, and data will be released at https://github.com/dsilvavinicius/m-plicits.

AI.tldr: M-plicits is a multiscale implicit neural representation framework for 3D surfaces that uses nested neighborhoods and residual MLP training to achieve noise-robust surface reconstruction with efficient real-time rendering.
AI.motivation: Existing INR methods struggle to balance training efficiency, rendering speed, and noise robustness. Single-MLPs are computationally expensive at inference, grid-based methods overfit noise and limit smoothness, and prior multiscale approaches suffer from hard spectral truncation artifacts.
AI.method: The proposed M-plicits framework models surfaces as a residual sum of MLPs trained via nested neighborhoods. Supervision is strictly localized to narrow bands around previous zero-level sets (unlike standard domain-wide sampling). The coarse network acts as a low-pass filter establishing a geometric prior, while residuals progressively refine geometry. Two technical contributions: (1) multiscale sphere-tracing algorithm, (2) GEMM-based analytical normal computation bypassing auto-differentiation.
AI.result: On Stanford and Thingi32 datasets: achieves best mean Chamfer distance (coarse config) and best median Chamfer distance + IoU (fine config). Significantly better noise robustness than iNGP, BACON, and IDF. Uses an order of magnitude fewer parameters than grid-based baselines.
AI.conclusion: M-plicits successfully addresses the noise robustness limitation of prior multiscale INR methods through its nested neighborhood design and residual training scheme, while maintaining computational efficiency through analytical normal computation and achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction quality.

title: UltraBench 2: Towards Robust Evaluation of Vision Foundation Models on Ultrasound
summary: Benchmarking is an increasingly critical part of research in machine learning and the domains where it is applied, including healthcare. Yet, despite the steady development of new ultrasound foundation models in recent years, the development of well-designed benchmarks to evaluate them has lagged behind. This deficiency has led to fragmented and inconsistent evaluations of competing models, making it difficult to measure progress. To address this issue, we introduce UltraBench 2, a comprehensive benchmark with wide anatomical and task coverage, and a focus on standardization, reproducibility, and ease-of-use. Using this benchmark, we compare existing vision foundation models for ultrasound image analysis. Our analyses demonstrate that ultrasound-specific pretraining still leads on classification, but that state-of-the-art general-purpose models have drawn level on segmentation.

AI.tldr: UltraBench 2 is introduced as a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating ultrasound vision foundation models, addressing the lack of standardized evaluation methods in the field. The benchmark covers wide anatomical and task coverage with focus on standardization, reproducibility, and ease-of-use.
AI.motivation: The research is motivated by the gap between the rapid development of ultrasound foundation models and the lack of well-designed benchmarks to evaluate them. This has led to fragmented and inconsistent evaluations of competing models, making it difficult to measure progress in the field.
AI.method: The researchers created UltraBench 2, a comprehensive benchmark with wide anatomical and task coverage, emphasizing standardization, reproducibility, and ease-of-use. They then used this benchmark to compare existing vision foundation models for ultrasound image analysis.
AI.result: The study found that ultrasound-specific pretraining still leads on classification tasks, but state-of-the-art general-purpose models have drawn level with ultrasound-specific models on segmentation tasks.
AI.conclusion: UltraBench 2 provides a standardized evaluation framework for ultrasound foundation models. The key conclusion is that while ultrasound-specific pretraining remains superior for classification, general-purpose models have caught up in segmentation performance, suggesting different model suitability depending on the task.

title: PePESeg3D: Perception Prior Enhances Multi-Scale Segmentation for 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: Recent advancements in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) have extended its capabilities to multi-scale segmentation. Existing methods reconstruct a scene with Gaussian primitives and learn multi-scale segmentation features separately, which leaves the geometry unaware of semantic structure and the feature learning dependent on incomplete mask supervision. To address these limitations, we present PePESeg3D, a novel framework that injects perception priors into a multi-scale 3D Gaussian segmentation pipeline. To fully exploit perception priors, we integrate them not only into contrastive feature learning but also into the upstream geometry reconstruction. Specifically, PePE Reconstruction incorporates monocular depth and mask constraints to ensure semantically coherent object structures. Building on this aligned geometry, PePE Contrastive Learning leverages dense depth-color cues and view-consistent centroid supervision to compensate for the incompleteness of multi-scale masks obtained from a 2D foundation model. Extensive experiments on the SPIn-NeRF, LERF-Mask, and NVOS benchmarks demonstrate that PePESeg3D achieves state-of-the-art performance in both multi-scale segmentation and scene reconstruction, highlighting the importance of integrating perception priors into both geometry optimization and feature learning for accurate multi-scale 3D segmentation. Our code is available at https://github.com/BeCow5X5/PePESeg3D.

AI.tldr: PePESeg3D introduces perception priors into multi-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting segmentation by integrating them into both geometry reconstruction (via monocular depth and mask constraints) and contrastive feature learning (via dense depth-color cues and view-consistent centroid supervision), achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing 3DGS multi-scale segmentation methods reconstruct scenes with Gaussian primitives and learn segmentation features separately, resulting in geometry that is unaware of semantic structure and feature learning that depends on incomplete mask supervision from 2D foundation models.
AI.method: PePESeg3D consists of two components: (1) PePE Reconstruction that incorporates monocular depth and mask constraints to ensure semantically coherent object structures; (2) PePE Contrastive Learning that leverages dense depth-color cues and view-consistent centroid supervision to compensate for incomplete multi-scale masks.
AI.result: PePESeg3D achieves state-of-the-art performance in both multi-scale segmentation and scene reconstruction on SPIn-NeRF, LERF-Mask, and NVOS benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Integrating perception priors into both geometry optimization and feature learning is crucial for accurate multi-scale 3D segmentation, demonstrating the importance of aligning geometry with semantic understanding.

title: GeoNLI - A Natural Language Interpreter for Satellite Imagery
summary:
Multi-modal multitasking models have shown strong performance on remote sensing datasets. However, because these models are trained on heterogeneous data and vary across tasks, designing a unified model that performs well in captioning, visual question answering (VQA), and visual grounding remains challenging.
  In this work, we evaluate several models on the VRS Bench and NWPU-VHR-10 datasets. The EarthMind model demonstrates strong results in both captioning and VQA. For grounding, we propose multiple pipelines - RemoteSAM-SAM-v1, RemoteSAM-SAM-v2, and DiffuSAM - and ultimately adopt a majority-voting ensemble across EarthMind, RemoteSAM, SAM3, Falcon, RemoteSAM-SAM3-v1, RemoteSAM-SAM3-v2, and DiffuSAM predictions.
  Our unified, modular pipeline integrates advanced SAM variants with multimodal LLMs to jointly perform captioning, VQA, and grounding. It achieves 82% accuracy on captioning and 83.32% on VQA, with 90.94%, 52.04%, and 92.06% for binary, numeric, and semantic question types respectively. For grounding, it attains 64.94% accuracy. By combining diverse VLMs with our custom RemoteSAM-SAM3 models through ensemble majority voting, the system delivers more accurate and consistent remote-sensing understanding than task-specific approaches.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a unified, modular pipeline for remote sensing visual understanding that jointly performs captioning, visual question answering (VQA), and visual grounding by integrating advanced SAM variants with multimodal LLMs through ensemble majority voting.
AI.motivation: Multi-modal multitasking models show strong performance on remote sensing datasets, but designing a unified model that performs well across captioning, VQA, and visual grounding remains challenging due to heterogeneous training data and task variations.
AI.method: The authors evaluated several models on VRS Bench and NWPU-VHR-10 datasets. They proposed multiple grounding pipelines (RemoteSAM-SAM-v1, RemoteSAM-SAM-v2, DiffuSAM) and adopted a majority-voting ensemble combining EarthMind, RemoteSAM, SAM3, Falcon, RemoteSAM-SAM3-v1, RemoteSAM-SAM3-v2, and DiffuSAM predictions.
AI.result: The unified pipeline achieves 82% accuracy on captioning, 83.32% on VQA (with 90.94%, 52.04%, and 92.06% for binary, numeric, and semantic question types respectively), and 64.94% accuracy on grounding.
AI.conclusion: By combining diverse VLMs with custom RemoteSAM-SAM3 models through ensemble majority voting, the system delivers more accurate and consistent remote sensing understanding than task-specific approaches.

title: Small yet Assistive: Spatially-Aware Post-Training for Low Vision
summary: An estimated 1 billion people worldwide live with vision impairment, yet current vision-language models (VLMs) produce descriptions too vague for safe navigation by blind and low-vision (BLV) users. Large VLMs can generate high-quality audio-description-compliant narrations but cannot run on mobile devices; small VLMs offer competitive latency but lack spatial detail, directional cues, and hazard awareness for navigational assistance. We present Smol-VL-BLV, a compact VLM for blind and low-vision users that closes this gap using a 500M decoder transformer model and two post-training mechanisms: (1) teacher-student distillation and (2) Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a composite BLV reward targeting directional language, metric distances, and hazard detection. Because multi-stage post-training can induce catastrophic forgetting, we add a lightweight finetuning stage after the last stage GRPO finetuning to recover general descriptive quality while preserving BLV-specific spatial grounding. Our best model substantially outperforms the baseline across various benchmarks, including tasks: VQA, BLV captioning, OCR, and latency. Compared with the baseline for relative improvement, it improves the Spatial score gain of 19.3%, and the Social score gain of 14.8%. It also increases OCR-Bench by 101.5%, and raises TextVQA accuracy by 44.2%. These results show that BLV-focused post-training improves both accessibility-specific spatial grounding and general visual-text reasoning. Deployed on a mid-range Android smartphone via Mixed-Precision Quantization, the model remains approx. 450 MB and runs entirely on-device, offline and without network dependency, generating descriptions with latency dependent on host hardware capabilities. Our model, dataset, and code is publicly released at https://smol-vl-blv.github.io/Smol-VL-BLV-website/

AI.tldr: Smol-VL-BLV is a compact 500M parameter vision-language model designed for blind and low-vision (BLV) users, achieving a balance between mobile deployability and spatial navigation capabilities. It uses teacher-student distillation and GRPO with BLV-specific rewards, plus a recovery finetuning stage to prevent catastrophic forgetting.
AI.motivation: Current vision-language models either produce descriptions too vague for safe BLV navigation (large models) or lack spatial detail, directional cues, and hazard awareness (small models). There is a need for a mobile-deployable VLM that provides detailed, actionable descriptions for BLV users' navigation needs.
AI.method: 1) Teacher-student distillation from large VLM to 500M decoder transformer; 2) Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with composite BLV reward targeting directional language, metric distances, and hazard detection; 3) Lightweight finetuning after GRPO to recover general descriptive quality while preserving BLV-specific spatial grounding. Model quantized and deployed on mid-range Android smartphone.
AI.result: Spatial score: +19.3%; Social score: +14.8%; OCR-Bench: +101.5%; TextVQA: +44.2%. Model size ~450 MB, runs entirely on-device offline on mid-range Android smartphone.
AI.conclusion: BLV-focused post-training improves both accessibility-specific spatial grounding and general visual-text reasoning. The model successfully bridges the gap between mobile deployability and detailed spatial descriptions needed for BLV navigation assistance.

title: DrGait: Biomechanically Grounded Visual Reasoning for Interpretable Clinical Gait Analysis
summary: Current automated gait analysis for clinical applications relies on uninterpretable black-box classifiers. Although Vision-Language Models (VLMs) offer strong reasoning capabilities, applying them directly to gait videos often leads to hallucinations, because they struggle to measure subtle geometric deviations from raw visual contexts. To address this, we introduce DrGait, a training-free agentic framework that shifts the VLM's role from a direct visual reasoner to a clinical planner. DrGait decouples semantic reasoning from geometric perception through a structured Triage-Verification-Synthesis (TVS) workflow. Given an input video and a set of basic spatiotemporal metrics, the DrGait agent first performs a heuristic triage to propose diagnostic hypotheses, which are then verified by autonomously calling deterministic biomechanical tools that operate on reconstructed 3D mesh trajectories, segmented 2D pose tracks, and event-centered video evidence. Finally, a closed-loop mechanism recursively updates the agent's reasoning context based on the feedback. By anchoring VLM's reasoning in verifiable geometric and temporal measurements, DrGait reduces hallucinations, achieving competitive diagnostic accuracy while generating transparent and audit-ready clinical reports.

AI.tldr: DrGait is a training-free agentic framework that addresses hallucinations in Vision-Language Models when applied to clinical gait analysis. It shifts VLM's role from direct visual reasoner to clinical planner by decoupling semantic reasoning from geometric perception through a Triage-Verification-Synthesis (TVS) workflow, anchoring VLM reasoning in verifiable biomechanical measurements.
AI.motivation: Current automated gait analysis for clinical applications relies on uninterpretable black-box classifiers. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) offer strong reasoning capabilities but struggle to measure subtle geometric deviations from raw visual contexts, leading to hallucinations when applied directly to gait videos.
AI.method: DrGait uses a structured Triage-Verification-Synthesis (TVS) workflow: (1) Heuristic triage proposes diagnostic hypotheses from input video and basic spatiotemporal metrics; (2) Verification through autonomous calls to deterministic biomechanical tools operating on reconstructed 3D mesh trajectories, segmented 2D pose tracks, and event-centered video evidence; (3) Closed-loop mechanism recursively updates reasoning context based on feedback.
AI.result: DrGait reduces hallucinations by anchoring VLM's reasoning in verifiable geometric and temporal measurements, while achieving competitive diagnostic accuracy and generating transparent, audit-ready clinical reports.
AI.conclusion: The training-free agentic framework successfully addresses VLM limitations in clinical gait analysis by decoupling semantic reasoning from geometric perception, providing interpretable and verifiable diagnostic outputs suitable for clinical applications.

title: DeltaWAM: Delta World Action Models for Bimanual Manipulation
summary: World-action models (WAMs) transfer visual and motion priors from pretrained video generators to robot control by jointly modeling visual dynamics and actions. Existing WAMs, however, predict dense future frames during training, repeatedly modeling largely unchanged content and coupling action-conditioned dynamics to nuisance appearance variations. At inference, processing each complete observation with the heavy video expert bottlenecks few-step action generation. Accordingly, we propose DeltaWAM, which jointly predicts visual deltas and actions using dense-anchor, sparse-delta, and action streams, with three architectures that differ in representation and computation sharing. We further develop Streaming Delta Memory (SDM), which updates cached anchor context with compact observed deltas, reducing heavy video-expert processing. On RoboTwin, DeltaWAM with SDM improves average success over Fast-WAM from 81.3% to 85.4% in the clean setting and from 75.8% to 83.9% under visual randomization. The three architectures reduce training FLOPs by 17.78-23.77%, while SDM reduces one-step inference latency and FLOPs by 36.57% and 31.55%, respectively; real-world evaluations further show the highest overall success rate and normalized progress among the evaluated policies. Code: https://github.com/AIGeeksGroup/DeltaWAM. Website: https://aigeeksgroup.github.io/DeltaWAM.

AI.tldr: DeltaWAM addresses inefficiencies in World-action models (WAMs) by predicting visual deltas and actions instead of dense future frames, and uses Streaming Delta Memory (SDM) to reduce heavy video-expert processing. This achieves 85.4% success rate (clean) and 83.9% (visual randomization) on RoboTwin, while reducing training FLOPs by 17.78-23.77% and inference FLOPs by 31.55%.
AI.motivation: Existing WAMs inefficiently predict dense future frames during training (modeling largely unchanged content), couple action-conditioned dynamics to nuisance appearance variations, and suffer from slow few-step action generation due to heavy video expert processing at inference.
AI.method: Proposed DeltaWAM with three architectures: (1) dense-anchor stream for anchor frames, (2) sparse-delta stream for change representation, and (3) action stream for control. Also developed Streaming Delta Memory (SDM) that updates cached anchor context with compact observed deltas to reduce heavy video-expert processing.
AI.result: On RoboTwin: DeltaWAM with SDM improves average success from 81.3% to 85.4% (clean setting) and from 75.8% to 83.9% (under visual randomization). Training FLOPs reduced by 17.78-23.77%. SDM reduces one-step inference latency and FLOPs by 36.57% and 31.55% respectively. Real-world evaluations show highest overall success rate and normalized progress.
AI.conclusion: DeltaWAM successfully addresses WAM inefficiencies through delta prediction and efficient anchor caching, achieving superior success rates in both simulation and real-world settings while significantly reducing computational costs.

title: CinematicVQA: Benchmarking Film-Grammar Reasoning in Large Vision-Language Models
summary: Cinematography, the craft of visual storytelling through framing, lighting, and camera operation, fundamentally shapes how audiences perceive and emotionally engage with video content. While Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) have made remarkable progress in video question answering, existing benchmarks primarily focus on identifying low-level techniques rather than understanding their storytelling impact. To address this, we introduce CinematicVQA, the first-of-its-kind benchmark for cinematic video understanding that goes beyond technique recognition to evaluate film-grammar reasoning, utilizing our introduced Cinematic Scene Graph (CSG), a structured representation that links filming techniques to their perceptual effects and narrative functions. Through comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LVLMs, we reveal a striking semantic gap: models consistently perform higher on describing visual presentations than on identifying the underlying techniques. Surprisingly, Chain-of-Thought prompting fails to provide consistent gains and degrades performance for most models, suggesting that current LVLMs lack sufficient cinematic domain knowledge to benefit from step-by-step reasoning. Fine-tuning on \textsc{CinematicVQA-train} yields consistent improvements, particularly for narrative function and multi-hop reasoning. Overall, \textsc{CinematicVQA} serves both as a rigorous benchmark for cinematic evaluation in LVLMs and as a practical dataset for training more film-aware video models.

AI.tldr: CinematicVQA is a new benchmark for evaluating LVLMs' understanding of cinematic video, using Cinematic Scene Graph (CSG) to link filming techniques to their perceptual effects and narrative functions. Evaluation reveals a semantic gap where models excel at describing visual presentations but struggle with technique identification, and that CoT prompting fails to provide consistent gains.
AI.motivation: Existing video understanding benchmarks focus only on low-level technique recognition, not on understanding the storytelling impact of cinematography. LVLMs need to go beyond identifying techniques to reasoning about their narrative and emotional effects.
AI.method: Introduced CinematicVQA benchmark with Cinematic Scene Graph (CSG) representation linking filming techniques to perceptual effects and narrative functions. Conducted comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LVLMs, tested Chain-of-Thought prompting, and fine-tuned models on CinematicVQA-train.
AI.result: Models perform better on describing visual presentations than identifying underlying techniques. CoT prompting fails to provide consistent gains and degrades performance for most models. Fine-tuning yields consistent improvements, particularly for narrative function and multi-hop reasoning.
AI.conclusion: CinematicVQA serves as both a rigorous benchmark for cinematic evaluation in LVLMs and a practical dataset for training more film-aware video models. Current LVLMs lack sufficient cinematic domain knowledge to benefit from step-by-step reasoning.

title: M$^2$PFN: End-to-End Disentangled Alignment for Generalizable Multimodal In-Context Learning in Alzheimer's Disease
summary: While various multimodal methods combining imaging and tabular data for Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis were proposed, they are often limited in generalization across cohorts. In-context learning (ICL) has demonstrated excellent generalization performances and high flexibility in foundational tabular models such as TabPFN. To extend TabPFN's ICL to multimodal AD analysis, the main obstacle is that TabPFN is meta-trained on synthetic tabular priors that do not naturally match the statistical structure of image-derived features. We propose M$^2$PFN, an end-to-end framework that turns this tabular foundation model into a multimodal AD predictor. M$^2$PFN (i) performs differentiable inference through TabPFN's transformer, back-propagating task gradients into 3D-MRI and tabular encoders; (ii) aligns the two modalities into a shared subspace, via disentanglement and a contrastive objective, matched to the ICL engine's prior; and (iii) folds in a frozen tabular-only prediction through a learnable gated shortcut. Because the ICL engine stays frozen, its in-context mechanism is preserved for test-time generalization, while end-to-end training shapes the encoders into features it can exploit. On ADNI ($n=2240$, three-class CN/MCI/AD), M$^2$PFN attains $65.55\%$ macro-F1 and $82.21\%$ macro-AUC, surpassing a comprehensive set of unimodal and multimodal baselines. By swapping only the head for a TabPFN regressor, the same architecture regresses baseline MMSE on a $1250$-subject sub-cohort to test MAE $1.743$, outperforming every multimodal baseline. On two external cohorts (OASIS-3 and SCAN) with no retraining, M$^2$PFN achieves the best AUC and the lowest MMSE MAE across all baselines, and transfers even when the cognitive instrument changes.

AI.tldr: M²PFN extends the in-context learning capability of TabPFN to multimodal Alzheimer's disease prediction by combining 3D-MRI and tabular data through a carefully designed alignment mechanism, achieving superior generalization across external cohorts compared to existing unimodal and multimodal baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal methods for AD diagnosis combine imaging and tabular data but suffer from poor generalization across different cohorts. While in-context learning (ICL) in foundation tabular models like TabPFN shows excellent generalization, it cannot directly handle multimodal data because TabPFN is meta-trained on synthetic tabular priors that don't match image-derived features.
AI.method: M²PFN employs three key mechanisms: (1) Differentiable inference through TabPFN's transformer, backpropagating task gradients into 3D-MRI and tabular encoders; (2) Alignment of both modalities into a shared subspace via disentanglement and contrastive objective, matched to ICL engine's prior; (3) A learnable gated shortcut that incorporates frozen tabular-only predictions. The ICL engine remains frozen to preserve its in-context mechanism for test-time generalization.
AI.result: On ADNI (n=2240, three-class CN/MCI/AD): 65.55% macro-F1, 82.21% macro-AUC, outperforming all baselines. For MMSE regression on 1250 subjects: MAE 1.743, outperforming all multimodal baselines. On external cohorts (OASIS-3 and SCAN) without retraining: best AUC and lowest MMSE MAE across all baselines, with successful transfer even when cognitive instruments change.
AI.conclusion: M²PFN successfully bridges the gap between tabular foundation models and multimodal medical imaging by preserving ICL capabilities while enabling effective cross-cohort generalization. The approach demonstrates that carefully designed modality alignment and preserving the frozen ICL engine are key to achieving robust AD prediction across diverse populations.

title: Looks the Same, Answers Differently: Flip-Direction Steering for Robust Vision-Language Reasoning
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) achieve strong visual reasoning performance, yet subtle changes from routine image capture and processing can alter their reasoning trajectories even when images appear nearly identical. In long-horizon generation, the resulting activation shifts may accumulate across decoding steps, progressively altering reasoning tokens and ultimately changing the final answer, a phenomenon referred to as answer flips. To address this instability, we propose FlipDir (Flip-Direction Steering), a training-free inference-time method that estimates a low-rank flip-inducing activation subspace from contrastive pairs of original and answer-flipping inputs and selectively steers hidden states during decoding. A margin-based gate limits subspace attenuation to uncertain decoding steps, recovering original predictions while preserving stable ones. To evaluate robustness beyond accuracy or consistency on fixed test sets, we introduce VisFlip, a benchmark framework that constructs evaluation groups for a target model and visual variation setting to separately assess recovery of original predictions and preservation of stable ones. VisFlip spans nine dataset-variation combinations across scientific reasoning, robot-scene understanding, and medical VQA, covering subtle visual variations common in each domain. Experiments across 18 settings demonstrate that FlipDir consistently outperforms existing methods on the combined recovery and preservation metric. We will make our code publicly available.

AI.tldr: FlipDir is a training-free inference-time method that addresses "answer flips" in Vision-Language Models - where subtle visual variations cause the model to change its final answer even when images appear nearly identical. The method estimates a flip-inducing activation subspace from contrastive pairs and uses a margin-based gate to selectively steer hidden states during decoding.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models can experience unstable reasoning when images undergo subtle changes during capture/processing, causing activation shifts to accumulate across decoding steps and ultimately changing the final answer (answer flips). Current evaluation metrics like accuracy or consistency on fixed test sets are insufficient for assessing robustness to these variations.
AI.method: FlipDir works by: (1) estimating a low-rank flip-inducing activation subspace from contrastive pairs of original and answer-flipping inputs, (2) selectively steering hidden states during decoding, and (3) using a margin-based gate to limit subspace attenuation to uncertain decoding steps, recovering original predictions while preserving stable ones.
AI.result: Experiments across 18 settings (9 dataset-variation combinations across scientific reasoning, robot-scene understanding, and medical VQA) demonstrate that FlipDir consistently outperforms existing methods on the combined recovery and preservation metric.
AI.conclusion: FlipDir provides an effective training-free solution for improving VLM stability against visual variations. The introduced VisFlip benchmark framework enables systematic evaluation of both recovery of original predictions and preservation of stable ones under various visual variation settings.

title: MEVL-STP: Multi-Encoder and Vision Language Model for Arbitrarily Shaped Scene Text Spotting
summary: Scene text spotting remains challenging for arbitrarily shaped text instances such as curved signs and dense multi-oriented characters in natural images, where tightly coupled architectures propagate localization errors directly into recognition failures. We present a two-stage pipeline that combines multi-encoder segmentation with vision-language model recognition to address this problem. In the detection stage, six frozen vision encoders (CLIP, DINOv2, SigLIP, EVA-CLIP, SAM, and ConvNeXt) extract complementary features spanning semantic, spatial, and texture spectra, which are fused through a trainable hierarchical Feature Pyramid Network with channel attention and decoded via a deep-supervision Progressive Scale Expansion network to generate precise instance-level text masks. By keeping the encoders frozen, their independently learned feature spaces remain orthogonal during fusion, preventing the feature homogenization that degrades boundary precision in single-backbone detectors. The detection stage produces tight polygon masks that conform to the actual shape of curved and arbitrarily oriented text, rather than axis-aligned rectangles that inevitably include background content. In the recognition stage, these polygon-masked crops isolate the target text from surrounding clutter, allowing a Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct model, fine-tuned via Low-Rank Adaptation on polygon-cropped scene text, to focus purely on reading the text without interference from neighbouring words or background noise. Without any synthetic pretraining data, our method achieves 91.99% detection F-measure and 85.86% end-to-end H-mean on CTW1500, setting a new state of the art and achieving strong performance on Total-Text and ICDAR 2015 without any synthetic training data. Code is available at https://github.com/doubleblind-afk/MEVL-STP

AI.tldr: A two-stage scene text spotting pipeline that combines multi-encoder segmentation with vision-language model recognition. Uses six frozen vision encoders for complementary feature extraction, fused via a hierarchical FPN with channel attention, followed by a deep-supervision Progressive Scale Expansion network for precise text mask generation. Recognition uses Qwen3-VL-8B fine-tuned via LoRA on polygon-cropped text.
AI.motivation: Scene text spotting faces challenges with arbitrarily shaped text (curved signs, dense multi-oriented characters) where tightly coupled architectures propagate localization errors directly into recognition failures. Existing methods suffer from feature homogenization that degrades boundary precision, and axis-aligned rectangles inevitably include background content.
AI.method: Detection Stage: Six frozen vision encoders (CLIP, DINOv2, SigLIP, EVA-CLIP, SAM, ConvNeXt) extract complementary features spanning semantic, spatial, and texture spectra. Features are fused through a trainable hierarchical Feature Pyramid Network with channel attention and decoded via a deep-supervision Progressive Scale Expansion network to generate precise instance-level text masks. Recognition Stage: Polygon-masked crops isolate target text, allowing Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct model fine-tuned via Low-Rank Adaptation to focus on reading text without interference.
AI.result: Achieves 91.99% detection F-measure and 85.86% end-to-end H-mean on CTW1500, setting a new state of the art. Also achieves strong performance on Total-Text and ICDAR 2015 without any synthetic training data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method successfully addresses arbitrarily shaped text detection through multi-encoder fusion with frozen backbones preserving orthogonal feature spaces. The two-stage pipeline with polygon-masked recognition enables precise text spotting without synthetic pretraining data, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks.

title: Multimodal Routing and Region Refinement for Language-Guided Medical Image Segmentation
comment: Accepted at MICCAI 2026 (TIA). Final version to appear in the proceedings
summary: Textual descriptions can reduce ambiguity in medical image segmentation by specifying the finding and location to be delineated. Existing text-guided methods mainly improve where image and language features interact but generally retain a single learned update pathway across all image-text pairs. We propose MRSeg, a parameter-efficient framework that uses each image-text pair to route the adaptation of visual and textual features before dense prediction. Frozen ConvNeXt-Tiny and PubMedBERT encoders provide multiscale visual features and clinical text tokens. A joint router uses the deepest visual feature and pooled text to predict a sparse mixture over low-rank adapter bases. The resulting route is shared across separate adapter banks for two visual scales and text, coordinating their adaptation while keeping the feature-specific parameters separate. Region Bridge uses text-derived queries to aggregate dense visual tokens into latent regions, refines these regions through self-attention and text cross-attention, and redistributes the refined information back to the feature maps. Finally, a multiscale decoder combines refined semantic features with shallow image evidence. On QaTa-COV19 and MosMedData+, MRSeg achieves 90.90/83.32 and 81.53/68.82 Dice/mIoU, respectively, with 7.11M trainable parameters and 7.60 GFLOPs. Code: https://github.com/maklachur/MRSeg.

AI.tldr: MRSeg is a parameter-efficient text-guided medical image segmentation framework that uses a joint router to predict sparse mixtures over low-rank adapter bases for adapting visual and textual features, with a Region Bridge module that aggregates visual tokens into latent regions refined through self-attention and text cross-attention.
AI.motivation: Existing text-guided medical image segmentation methods mainly improve where image and language features interact but generally retain a single learned update pathway across all image-text pairs, lacking dynamic adaptation per input pair.
AI.method: Frozen ConvNeXt-Tiny and PubMedBERT encoders provide multiscale visual features and clinical text tokens. A joint router uses the deepest visual feature and pooled text to predict a sparse mixture over low-rank adapter bases, shared across separate adapter banks for two visual scales and text. Region Bridge uses text-derived queries to aggregate dense visual tokens into latent regions, refines them through self-attention and text cross-attention, then redistributes refined information back to feature maps. A multiscale decoder combines refined semantic features with shallow image evidence.
AI.result: On QaTa-COV19: 90.90 Dice, 83.32 mIoU. On MosMedData+: 81.53 Dice, 68.82 mIoU. Uses 7.11M trainable parameters and 7.60 GFLOPs.
AI.conclusion: MRSeg achieves state-of-the-art performance on two medical image segmentation datasets (QaTa-COV19 and MosMedData+) with a parameter-efficient design using only 7.11M trainable parameters and 7.60 GFLOPs, demonstrating effective coordination between visual and textual features through dynamic routing and region-based aggregation.

title: Direction-Scale Decomposition in Action Representation: Rethinking What to Tokenize for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Action representation plays a central role in discrete-token vision-language-action (VLA) learning but remains underexamined. Under conventional pose-increment representations, action tokens are sensitive to execution speed and dataset-specific normalization, potentially obscuring geometric structure shared across demonstrations and datasets. We introduce Direction-Scale Decomposition (DSD), an action representation that decomposes translation and rotation increments into direction and scale components before tokenization. DSD isolates motion direction while retaining magnitudes in separate scale channels. We evaluate DSD with uniform binning (BIN) and BEAST, a B-spline-based tokenizer, in simulation and real-world manipulation under both single-dataset and mixed-dataset training. On LIBERO, DSD improves average success rates with both tokenizers. On SimplerEnv, DSD-BIN outperforms BIN by 10.3 percentage points in overall success rate under mixed-dataset training. Real-robot experiments further show gains both with and without robotics pretraining. These results support DSD as an effective action representation for discrete-token VLA models and suggest its potential to mitigate performance degradation when training on large and diverse dataset mixtures. Our project page with additional resources is available at https://vla-dsd.github.io/

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Direction-Scale Decomposition (DSD), a novel action representation for discrete-token vision-language-action (VLA) models that decomposes translation and rotation increments into direction and scale components before tokenization. DSD isolates motion direction while retaining magnitudes in separate scale channels, addressing limitations of conventional pose-increment representations that are sensitive to execution speed and dataset-specific normalization.
AI.motivation: The core problem is that conventional pose-increment representations in VLA learning are sensitive to execution speed and dataset-specific normalization, which obscures geometric structure shared across demonstrations and datasets. This limits the model's ability to generalize across different datasets and execution conditions.
AI.method: The proposed DSD method decomposes translation and rotation increments into direction and scale components before tokenization. The method is evaluated with two tokenizers: (1) uniform binning (BIN) and (2) BEAST, a B-spline-based tokenizer. Experiments are conducted in simulation (LIBERO, SimplerEnv) and real-world manipulation settings, under both single-dataset and mixed-dataset training scenarios.
AI.result: On LIBERO, DSD improves average success rates with both tokenizers. On SimplerEnv, DSD-BIN outperforms BIN by 10.3 percentage points in overall success rate under mixed-dataset training. Real-robot experiments demonstrate gains both with and without robotics pretraining, showing DSD's effectiveness across varied training conditions.
AI.conclusion: DSD is an effective action representation for discrete-token VLA models. It can mitigate performance degradation when training on large and diverse dataset mixtures, suggesting potential for improving generalization in robotics learning from diverse data sources.

title: ViRDM: Taming Representation Distribution Matching for Few-Step Causal Video Generation
summary: Few-step autoregressive (AR) video diffusion enables low-latency streaming generation, but existing post-training methods predominantly rely on Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD), requiring both a large pretrained teacher and an online critic to estimate distributional discrepancies through diffusion scores. In this work, we ask whether this resource-intensive teacher--critic stack can be eliminated by post-training only the generator against a precomputed target distribution. Drawing inspiration from representation distribution matching (RDM) for one-step image generation, we systematically study its transfer to few-step causal video generation and identify three key barriers: a memory-intractable gradient path, a distinct video optimization regime, and representation distributions that underconstrain temporal dynamics. We introduce ViRDM, a teacher- and critic-free video post-training recipe that addresses these barriers sequentially. By coupling RDM with stochastically truncated clean-exit supervision, a lightweight VAE decoder, and staged vector--Jacobian products, ViRDM makes representation distribution matching memory-feasible for multi-step causal video rollouts. We further establish effective generated-population and initialization regimes for video RDM, and introduce lightweight dynamics regularization to compensate for the underconstrained temporal dynamics. ViRDM turns three-network distillation into generator-only post-training, reducing GPU memory use and training time while improving video quality. With only 20 generator updates, the recipe reaches 84.87 on the official VBench evaluation, outperforming the previous best few-step causal baseline by 0.36, while requiring 16 A100 GPU-hours. We additionally report exploratory results demonstrating the potential of the same recipe for lower causal sampling budget and for one-, two-, and four-step bidirectional generation.

AI.tldr: ViRDM is a teacher- and critic-free post-training method for few-step autoregressive video generation that achieves 84.87 on VBench by using representation distribution matching (RDM) with innovations including stochastically truncated clean-exit supervision, lightweight VAE decoder, staged vector-Jacobian products, and dynamics regularization, reducing GPU memory and training time while outperforming previous best by 0.36.
AI.motivation: Existing post-training methods for few-step AR video diffusion rely on Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) which requires both a large pretrained teacher and an online critic to estimate distributional discrepancies through diffusion scores. This resource-intensive teacher-critic stack motivates the search for a simpler, generator-only post-training approach against a precomputed target distribution.
AI.method: ViRDM addresses three key barriers in transferring RDM from one-step image generation to few-step causal video generation: (1) memory-intractable gradient path - solved via staged vector-Jacobian products; (2) distinct video optimization regime - addressed by establishing effective generated-population and initialization regimes; (3) underconstrained temporal dynamics - compensated by lightweight dynamics regularization. The method combines RDM with stochastically truncated clean-exit supervision and a lightweight VAE decoder.
AI.result: With only 20 generator updates, ViRDM reaches 84.87 on the official VBench evaluation, outperforming the previous best few-step causal baseline by 0.36. Training requires only 16 A100 GPU-hours, significantly reducing GPU memory use and training time compared to three-network distillation approaches.
AI.conclusion: ViRDM successfully eliminates the need for teacher and critic networks in few-step video generation post-training, achieving superior video quality with minimal computational resources. The approach demonstrates potential for lower causal sampling budgets and multi-step bidirectional generation scenarios.

title: PlenoCI: Plenoptic CharacterIstics for View Dependence Aware Change Classification
summary: Radiance field representations such as 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) natively encode complex visual phenomena such as occlusions and view dependence, but they are inherently underconstrained. Independently optimized reconstructions converge to different primitive configurations, even in unchanged regions. We introduce Plenoptic CharacterIstics (PlenoCI), a novel feature built from the plenoptic field these representations approximate. PlenoCI directly captures rich visual behaviors while ignoring Lambertian textures. By deriving closed-form analytic plenoptic derivatives from a 3DGS representation, we efficiently detect these 5D structures. Our approach is robust to underconstrained representations by construction, reporting two orders of magnitude fewer false positives between independent reconstructions of unchanged scenes than concurrent work. We demonstrate PlenoCI's utility on change classification. First, we detect changes with an instance-aware 3DGS pipeline, achieving state-of-the-art results on CL-Splats with a 25.7% mIoU gain over the strongest competitor, while remaining competitive on the more challenging PASLCD benchmark. Leveraging PlenoCI, we classify changes as geometric or appearance-based with a balanced accuracy of 0.735, comparable to the best performing baseline. We believe plenoptic derivatives and PlenoCI open new directions for view dependence aware understanding in visually complex environments. Code and data are available at https://js0n-lai.github.io/plenoci.

AI.tldr: PlenoCI is a novel feature derived from plenoptic field derivatives of 3D Gaussian Splatting representations that captures rich visual behaviors (occlusions, view dependence) while ignoring Lambertian textures. It enables robust change detection in underconstrained radiance field reconstructions.
AI.motivation: Radiance field representations like 3D Gaussian Splatting are inherently underconstrained, causing independently optimized reconstructions to converge to different primitive configurations even in unchanged regions, leading to false positives in change detection tasks.
AI.method: The method derives closed-form analytic plenoptic derivatives from a 3DGS representation to efficiently detect 5D plenoptic structures. This approach captures view-dependent visual phenomena while filtering out Lambertian textures, making it robust to underconstrained representations by construction.
AI.result: PlenoCI achieves two orders of magnitude fewer false positives between independent reconstructions compared to concurrent work. On CL-Splats, it achieves state-of-the-art results with a 25.7% mIoU gain over the strongest competitor. On PASLCD benchmark, it remains competitive. For change classification (geometric vs. appearance-based), it achieves a balanced accuracy of 0.735.
AI.conclusion: Plenoptic derivatives and PlenoCI open new directions for view-dependence aware understanding in visually complex environments, providing a robust solution for change detection in radiance field representations.

title: HelloWorld: Towards Practical Applications of Generative Driving World Models
summary: Driving world models provide a promising route toward scalable counterfactual data generation and interactive simulation beyond recorded driving logs. Realizing this potential requires a system that can generalize across diverse scenes, respond faithfully to prescribed controls, generate coherent multi-sensor observations, and operate efficiently under repeated inference. We present \textbf{HelloWorld}, a 2B driving world model system designed around these requirements. HelloWorld progressively specializes broad visual and motion priors from heterogeneous video data into controllable driving generation using ego pose, HD maps, and 3D boxes. A block-causal generation interface, together with adaptation to self-generated context, aligns the model with sequential simulation. The system further supports synchronized seven-camera RGB generation and conditional LiDAR synthesis, and is distilled toward few-step inference for efficient deployment. Experiments evaluate visual quality, control fidelity, cross-view consistency, robustness under repeated generation, inference efficiency, and LiDAR synthesis. Together, HelloWorld provides a unified framework for scalable driving data generation and interactive simulation.

AI.tldr: HelloWorld is a 2B parameter driving world model system that generates可控 driving scenarios using ego pose, HD maps, and 3D boxes. It supports synchronized seven-camera RGB generation and conditional LiDAR synthesis, with block-causal generation interface and few-step inference optimization for efficient deployment.
AI.motivation: Driving world models offer scalable counterfactual data generation and interactive simulation beyond recorded driving logs, but require generalization across diverse scenes, faithful control response, coherent multi-sensor observations, and efficient repeated inference.
AI.method: HelloWorld progressively specializes broad visual and motion priors from heterogeneous video data into controllable driving generation using ego pose, HD maps, and 3D boxes. It employs a block-causal generation interface with adaptation to self-generated context for sequential simulation, and is distilled for few-step inference.
AI.result: Experiments evaluate visual quality, control fidelity, cross-view consistency, robustness under repeated generation, inference efficiency, and LiDAR synthesis, demonstrating a unified framework for scalable driving data generation and interactive simulation.
AI.conclusion: HelloWorld provides a unified framework that addresses the requirements of scalable driving data generation and interactive simulation through multi-sensor support, efficient inference, and coherent generation across diverse scenarios.

title: Exploiting Target Knowledge from MLLMs for Robust Few-Shot Segmentation
summary: Few-shot segmentation (FSS) aims to segment unseen object categories with a few (e.g., one or five) labeled examples, enabling efficient adaptation to novel classes. Conventional models typically rely on appearance-based visual matching between support and query images for segmentation. While straightforward, these methods often struggle to handle significant appearance discrepancies and occlusions in the query image due to insufficient target knowledge. To mitigate this, we introduce a novel framework that mines target knowledge using the strong reasoning capacity of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) and employs it to enhance FSS. Specifically, building on SAM 2, our method, named MK-FSS, exploits two forms of complementary knowledge derived from a query image by an MLLM for FSS, including spatial knowledge, which provides a spatial prior indicating the potential target location, and semantic knowledge, which describes the target using text. The spatial knowledge is first encoded into a memory representation, and then resulting memory is integrated with the support-guided memory feature from query image through a carefully designed dual-memory debate-fusion (DMDF) module, yielding a more robust target memory feature. In parallel, the semantic knowledge is encoded into the textual feature, which is fused with multi-scale query features via a progressive cross-modal prompt generator (PCPG), producing a target-aware multimodal prompt for segmentation. Working together, the dual-memory feature and the multimodal prompt provide a comprehensive representation of the target, enabling more robust segmentation. In our extensive experiments, MK-FSS shows promising results and largely surpasses existing methods. Code will be released.

AI.tldr: MK-FSS is a novel few-shot segmentation framework that leverages Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to extract spatial and semantic knowledge from query images, integrating this information through dual-memory debate-fusion and cross-modal prompt generation modules built on SAM 2.
AI.motivation: Conventional few-shot segmentation methods rely on appearance-based visual matching between support and query images, which struggles to handle significant appearance discrepancies and occlusions due to insufficient target knowledge.
AI.method: The proposed MK-FSS framework extracts two forms of complementary knowledge from query images using an MLLM: (1) spatial knowledge providing spatial prior for target location, encoded into memory representation and integrated with support-guided memory via a Dual-Memory Debate-Fusion (DMDF) module; (2) semantic knowledge describing the target in text, encoded and fused with multi-scale query features through a Progressive Cross-Modal Prompt Generator (PCPG) to produce a target-aware multimodal prompt.
AI.result: MK-FSS shows promising results and largely surpasses existing methods in extensive experiments.
AI.conclusion: The combination of dual-memory feature and multimodal prompt provides a comprehensive target representation, enabling more robust segmentation of unseen object categories with only a few labeled examples.

title: MoVISA: Multi-Token Reasoning for Video Object Segmentation
summary: Recent advances in video object segmentation with Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) reasoning have demonstrated the effectiveness of using a single textual token, such as SEG, to predict segmentation masks across images and videos. However, we observe that this single-token strategy lacks the granularity required to precisely localize multiple objects across time in video segmentation tasks. To address this limitation, we develop Multi-Token Reasoning for Video Object Segmentation, or MoVISA. MoVISA uses multiple segmentation tokens, such as SEG0 and SEG1, to represent an object across different frames. This design enables more fine-grained alignment between language prompts and spatio-temporal mask predictions, improving both performance and interpretability. On the challenging MeViS, DAVIS17, ReVOS, and Ref-Youtube-VOS benchmarks, our model achieves a 13.2 percent J and F improvement on MeViS and an 8.4 percent J and F improvement on ReVOS. Code and models will be released.

AI.tldr: MoVISA introduces multi-token reasoning for video object segmentation, using segmentation tokens like SEG0 and SEG1 instead of a single SEG token to enable fine-grained alignment between language prompts and spatio-temporal mask predictions.
AI.motivation: Current MLLM-based video object segmentation methods use a single textual token (e.g., SEG) to predict segmentation masks, but this approach lacks the granularity needed to precisely localize multiple objects across time in video segmentation tasks.
AI.method: MoVISA uses multiple segmentation tokens (SEG0, SEG1, etc.) to represent objects across different frames, enabling more fine-grained alignment between language prompts and spatio-temporal mask predictions. This improves both performance and interpretability.
AI.result: On challenging benchmarks (MeViS, DAVIS17, ReVOS, and Ref-Youtube-VOS), MoVISA achieves a 13.2% J and F improvement on MeViS and an 8.4% J and F improvement on ReVOS.
AI.conclusion: Multi-token reasoning effectively addresses the limitation of single-token strategies in video object segmentation, providing superior performance and interpretability for tracking multiple objects across time.

title: Passive LWIR Hyperspectral Ranging via Transmittance Extraction and Distance Alignment
summary: Passive long-wave infrared (LWIR) hyperspectral ranging enables distance estimation in low-light and nighttime scenes by exploiting atmospheric absorption features in thermal radiance received through the atmosphere.Joint estimation of temperature, emissivity, and distance is computationally expensive. Reference-range joint inversion also uses a distance-invariant effective attenuation coefficient, which can bias range estimates.We introduce transmittance extraction and distance alignment (TEDA), which decouples range estimation from temperature--emissivity inversion. In the first stage, a baseline estimator with a data-fidelity term invariant to the known absorption direction yields two closed-form smoothing branches for the slowly varying thermal continuum. An observation-derived gate combines the branches, and subtracting the blended baseline in the log domain recovers atmospheric transmittance. The second stage estimates range by matching the recovered transmittance to sensor-domain transmittance models recomputed for each candidate distance. Monte Carlo simulations show that TEDA effectively reduces the ranging bias caused by the distance-invariant attenuation coefficient approximation. In a measured scene, TEDA's mean range estimates are closer to the LiDAR medians than those of reference-range joint inversion in both evaluated patches. TEDA processes a complete $256\times256$ region of interest in 8.19~s versus 159.47~s for reference-range joint inversion, an approximately 20-fold speedup.

title: Beneath the Scores: Rethinking Hallucination Evaluation for Video Understanding Models
summary:
Video understanding is increasingly performed by multi-stage LLM agents that separate temporal grounding, visual observation, and reasoning. Yet these stages are typically evaluated on different benchmarks and distributions, making it difficult to determine where hallucinations originate. We first organize existing benchmarks around these stages and show that their scores provide inconsistent diagnostic signals: stronger stage-level performance does not reliably imply lower downstream hallucination, and even benchmarks targeting the same capability can disagree.
  We therefore introduce a causal stage-intervention protocol that overwrites individual stages while holding the downstream task fixed. Across 60,008 runs on three video-agent architectures, we find that grounding is the dominant source of downstream error, with roughly four times the causal impact of corrupting visual observations. Successful grounding depends primarily on locating the correct region rather than precise temporal overlap, explaining why standard mIoU metrics poorly predict downstream reliability. We further find that incorrect evidence is substantially more harmful than missing evidence. Finally, auditing existing benchmarks against these interventions reveals that their scores do not reliably predict causal cascade sensitivity and can fail under distribution shift. These results motivate intervention-based, stage-aware evaluation for trustworthy video agents.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a causal stage-intervention protocol to diagnose hallucination sources in multi-stage video LLM agents. By conducting 60,008 runs across three architectures, the authors find that temporal grounding is the dominant source of downstream error, with grounding errors causing roughly four times more harm than visual observation errors. The paper also reveals that existing benchmarks provide inconsistent diagnostic signals and do not reliably predict causal cascade sensitivity.
AI.motivation: Multi-stage video LLM agents typically separate temporal grounding, visual observation, and reasoning into different stages. However, these stages are evaluated on different benchmarks, making it difficult to identify where hallucinations originate. The key problem is that stronger stage-level performance does not reliably imply lower downstream hallucination, and even benchmarks targeting the same capability can disagree.
AI.method: The authors introduce a causal stage-intervention protocol that overwrites individual stages while holding the downstream task fixed. They conducted experiments across 60,008 runs on three video-agent architectures, systematically intervening at each stage to measure causal impact on downstream errors.
AI.result: Key findings: (1) Grounding is the dominant source of downstream error, with roughly four times the causal impact of corrupting visual observations; (2) Successful grounding depends primarily on locating the correct region rather than precise temporal overlap (explaining why standard mIoU metrics poorly predict downstream reliability); (3) Incorrect evidence is substantially more harmful than missing evidence; (4) Existing benchmarks do not reliably predict causal cascade sensitivity and can fail under distribution shift.
AI.conclusion: The results motivate intervention-based, stage-aware evaluation for trustworthy video agents. Standard benchmark scores provide inconsistent diagnostic signals, and the community should adopt intervention-based evaluation methods to more accurately identify and address hallucination sources in video understanding systems.

title: Only What Was Seen: Observation-Gram Compaction of View-Dependent Appearance in 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: Most of the memory of a 3D Gaussian Splatting model holds spherical-harmonic colour coefficients, yet each Gaussian is seen only from the narrow cone of directions of the training cameras. We turn this into a distortion metric that other compressors can adopt: a per-Gaussian observation Gram matrix, accumulated from viewing directions and blending weights, is the exact first-order map from coefficient changes to squared image error and needs only the model and the camera poses. Under it, degree reduction becomes a closed-form projection that generalises truncation, degree allocation a Lagrangian rate-distortion problem, and vector quantisation the matrix-weighted Lloyd algorithm, of which Compressed3D's quantiser is the scalar case. Swapped into Compressed3D with everything else unchanged, the metric raises PSNR by +0.49 dB before fine-tuning, with SSIM and LPIPS following, and at matched rate still gains +0.32 dB without a single training image. A training-free stack built on the metric alone is 15% smaller than the image-free GSICO at equal quality on Mip-NeRF 360.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a distortion metric for 3D Gaussian Splatting compression based on per-Gaussian observation Gram matrices, which enables degree reduction, degree allocation, and vector quantisation optimizations. The method improves PSNR by +0.49 dB in Compressed3D and achieves 15% smaller size than GSICO at equal quality.
AI.motivation: Most memory in 3D Gaussian Splatting models is consumed by spherical-harmonic colour coefficients, yet each Gaussian is observed only from limited viewing directions of training cameras. This creates an opportunity to develop a more efficient compression metric that accounts for actual observation patterns.
AI.method: The authors propose a per-Gaussian observation Gram matrix accumulated from viewing directions and blending weights, which serves as the exact first-order map from coefficient changes to squared image error. This metric enables: (1) degree reduction as a closed-form projection generalizing truncation, (2) degree allocation as a Lagrangian rate-distortion problem, and (3) vector quantisation as the matrix-weighted Lloyd algorithm.
AI.result: When integrated into Compressed3D, the metric raises PSNR by +0.49 dB before fine-tuning, with SSIM and LPIPS improving accordingly. At matched rate, it gains +0.32 dB without any training images. A training-free stack built on this metric alone is 15% smaller than image-free GSICO at equal quality on Mip-NeRF 360.
AI.conclusion: The observation Gram matrix provides an effective distortion metric for 3D Gaussian Splatting compression that generalizes existing techniques like Compressed3D's quantiser. It enables significant quality improvements without requiring training images and achieves superior compression efficiency compared to prior methods.

title: FluidRain: Incompressible Rain Flow as an Attention Bias for Loop-in-Loop Video Deraining
summary: Existing video deraining methods typically exploit neighboring frames through either explicit alignment or implicit spatiotemporal aggregation. Explicit alignment relies on accurate motion estimation, which can become unreliable under dense rain, while implicit aggregation avoids alignment but lacks explicit guidance on the directional and temporally coherent structure of rain. This leaves a gap between reliable temporal aggregation and explicit modeling of rain motion. To address these limitations, we propose FluidRain, a lightweight video derainer that uses divergence-free rain flow to guide Loop-in-Loop attention across scales and neighboring frames. Motivated by fluid mechanics, we model rain motion as a divergence-free image-space flow and use it to organize multi-scale and temporal aggregation. Specifically, FluidRain first estimates a rain-flow field for each frame and projects it onto the divergence-free subspace. The resulting flow steers window attention along rain streaks, enabling neighboring frames to be aggregated without explicit alignment. Since rain-flow structure is preserved across scales and nearby frames, Loop-in-Loop reuses the same attention operator across both dimensions, resulting in a three-frame model with only 0.80M parameters. Experiments on four benchmarks show that FluidRain remains competitive with substantially larger restoration models. We further examine how temporal evidence scales with different input views. To evaluate whether the model remains reliable when rain motion changes across frames, we introduce RainSyn-Gust, which injects controlled changes in rain-streak direction into existing benchmarks. We also develop a physics-based no-reference metric that evaluates real-rain removal without requiring clean targets.

AI.tldr: FluidRain is a lightweight video deraining method (0.80M parameters) that uses divergence-free rain flow to guide Loop-in-Loop attention across scales and frames, avoiding explicit motion alignment while preserving rain structure modeling.
AI.motivation: Existing video deraining methods suffer from a trade-off: explicit alignment relies on unreliable motion estimation under dense rain, while implicit aggregation lacks explicit guidance on rain's directional and temporally coherent structure. This creates a gap between reliable temporal aggregation and explicit rain motion modeling.
AI.method:
1) Estimate rain-flow field for each frame and project onto divergence-free subspace
2) Use the resulting flow to steer window attention along rain streaks
3) Apply Loop-in-Loop attention operator across both scale and temporal dimensions
4) Three-frame model with shared attention across scales and frames
AI.result: Competitive with substantially larger restoration models on four benchmarks. Introduces RainSyn-Gust dataset for testing rain direction changes and a physics-based no-reference metric for real-world evaluation.
AI.conclusion: The divergence-free rain flow approach successfully bridges the gap between temporal aggregation and explicit rain motion modeling, achieving strong performance with a lightweight model. The proposed dataset and metric enable more comprehensive evaluation under varying rain conditions.

title: RGBD20K: A Large-Scale Benchmark for RGB-D Semantic Segmentation
summary: In this paper, we propose RGBD20K, a novel dataset for facilitating the development of more robust and general RGB-D semantic segmentation by encompassing abundant categories and high-quality annotations. RGBD20K possesses several attractive properties: (1) Expanded Semantic Space. In particular, it covers 160 fine-grained categories, largely surpassing the category diversity of existing popular RGB-D benchmarks (e.g., NYUv2 with 40 classes and SUN RGB-D with 37 classes). With such enriched semantic coverage, we expect to promote the learning of more generalizable segmentation models. (2) Larger Scale. Compared with current benchmarks, RGBD20K offers 20,000 RGB-D image pairs, providing a substantially larger training resource that benefits the development of more powerful deep models. (3) High-Fidelity Annotation. We perform rigorous re-evaluation and correction of existing labels to resolve long-standing annotation noise, resulting in a clean and reliable ground-truth foundation. Furthermore, we propose a novel score-purified fusion (SPF) method, which achieves state-of-the-art performance across all evaluated benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach in leveraging high-quality multimodal information for RGB-D semantic segmentation. The dataset is here: https://github.com/ShaohuaDong2021/RGBD20K/.

AI.tldr: RGBD20K is a large-scale RGB-D semantic segmentation dataset with 20,000 image pairs covering 160 categories, designed to address limitations in existing benchmarks (NYUv2 with 40 classes, SUN RGB-D with 37 classes). The authors also propose a score-purified fusion (SPF) method achieving state-of-the-art performance.
AI.motivation: Existing RGB-D semantic segmentation datasets suffer from limited category diversity (40 classes in NYUv2, 37 in SUN RGB-D) and annotation noise issues. The authors aim to create a more robust and generalizable dataset by expanding semantic coverage and improving annotation quality.
AI.method: The authors: (1) Created RGBD20K with 160 fine-grained categories and 20,000 RGB-D image pairs; (2) Performed rigorous re-evaluation and correction of existing labels to reduce annotation noise; (3) Proposed a novel score-purified fusion (SPF) method for leveraging multimodal information.
AI.result: RGBD20K significantly surpasses existing benchmarks in category diversity (160 vs 40/37 classes) and scale (20,000 images). The SPF method achieves state-of-the-art performance across all evaluated benchmarks, demonstrating effective use of high-quality multimodal information.
AI.conclusion: RGBD20K addresses key limitations in existing RGB-D semantic segmentation datasets by providing expanded semantic space, larger scale, and high-fidelity annotations. The proposed SPF method validates the dataset's value by achieving superior segmentation performance.

title: To Trust or Not to Trust: Retrieval-Augmented Fact Checking in Speech
summary: Online misinformation increasingly appears in spoken formats such as news clips, podcasts, interviews, political speeches, and social media videos, creating a need for fact-checking systems that can verify claims directly from speech. We introduce VeriSpeak, a probe benchmark for studying speech-based fact verification in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs). VeriSpeak contains 3,879 spoken claims spanning temporal, geographical, and relational facts, with balanced true and false labels. The benchmark is designed to examine whether factual verification ability transfers from text to speech, and whether retrieval-augmented LALMs can use textual evidence to correctly support or refute spoken claims.
