Our experiments reveal a consistent text-speech modality gap: LALMs that verify written claims reliably often fail on the same claims when spoken. Moreover, retrieval alone provides limited gains because models frequently conflate retrieved evidence with the spoken claim. In contrast, retrieval combined with explicit reasoning improves claim-evidence comparison, with a thinking-tuned LALM reaching 86.1% accuracy. VeriSpeak highlights that effective speech misinformation detection requires not only speech understanding, but also grounded reasoning over retrieved evidence. The dataset is publicly available via Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/abhiram4572/VeriSpeak.

AI.tldr: VeriSpeak is a benchmark for evaluating speech-based fact verification in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs), containing 3,879 spoken claims with balanced true/false labels across temporal, geographical, and relational facts. It tests whether factual verification abilities transfer from text to speech and whether retrieval-augmented LALMs can use textual evidence to verify spoken claims.
AI.motivation: The proliferation of misinformation in spoken formats (news clips, podcasts, speeches, social media videos) creates an urgent need for fact-checking systems that can verify claims directly from speech, rather than relying on manual transcription.
AI.method: The benchmark examines: (1) whether fact-checking ability transfers from text to speech in LALMs, and (2) whether retrieval-augmented LALMs can use textual evidence to support or refute spoken claims. Experiments tested multiple LALMs with different configurations including retrieval-only and retrieval plus explicit reasoning.
AI.result: A consistent text-speech modality gap was identified: LALMs that reliably verify written claims often fail on the same claims when spoken. Retrieval alone provides limited gains because models frequently conflate retrieved evidence with spoken claims. However, retrieval combined with explicit reasoning significantly improves claim-evidence comparison, with a thinking-tuned LALM achieving 86.1% accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Effective speech misinformation detection requires not only speech understanding but also grounded reasoning over retrieved evidence. The combination of retrieval and explicit reasoning is crucial for LALMs to accurately verify spoken claims.

title: Exploiting answer-invariant redundancies in satellite imagery for efficient VLM inference on edge
summary: Onboard vision-language models could enable satellites to answer queries directly, but exhaustive tiled inference over high-resolution imagery is slow and energy-intensive. We identify answer-invariant token redundancy (AITR): image tiles and vision tokens that can be removed without changing the final answer. We present Rift, a two-stage system that performs query-conditioned tile pruning followed by elastic prefill to reduce token budget. We evaluate it on LLaVA-1.5 7B running on Jetson AGX Orin. Compared with exhaustive tiled inference, Rift reduces energy by 78% and latency by 69%, while increasing accuracy from 45% to 73%.

AI.tldr: Rift is a two-stage system that reduces computational costs of onboard vision-language models on satellites by identifying and removing answer-invariant tokens. It combines query-conditioned tile pruning with elastic prefill, achieving 78% energy reduction, 69% latency reduction, and accuracy improvement from 45% to 73% on LLaVA-1.5 7B.
AI.motivation: Onboard vision-language models could enable satellites to answer queries directly, but exhaustive tiled inference over high-resolution imagery is slow and energy-intensive. There is a need to reduce computational burden while maintaining or improving accuracy.
AI.method: Rift introduces the concept of Answer-Invariant Token Redundancy (AITR) - image tiles and vision tokens that can be removed without changing the final answer. It uses a two-stage approach: (1) query-conditioned tile pruning to identify and remove irrelevant tiles, and (2) elastic prefill to reduce token budget.
AI.result: Evaluated on LLaVA-1.5 7B running on Jetson AGX Orin, Rift reduces energy by 78% and latency by 69%, while increasing accuracy from 45% to 73% compared to exhaustive tiled inference.
AI.conclusion: Rift successfully demonstrates that significant computational savings can be achieved on onboard vision-language models by leveraging answer-invariant token redundancy, with improvements in both efficiency and accuracy.

title: Where Hallucinations Live: A Cross-Architecture Circuit in VQ-Tokenized Vision-Language Models
summary: Unified vision-language models (VLMs) that tokenize images through a vector-quantized (VQ) codebook routinely hallucinate objects on grounded yes/no benchmarks, yet existing decoding-time fixes treat this as generic miscalibration without an architectural account. Using activation patching across twenty-five models spanning eight LLM families, we identify an early-layer ($L_0$) attention routing circuit shared across VQ-tokenized VLMs and propose a three-gate diagnostic that distinguishes the models carrying it from those that do not. The diagnostic isolates ten positive models (five natural unified-VQ VLMs across three LLM families and five induced variants) and rejects the remaining fifteen. A single-variable architectural swap (LLaVA-1.6 CLIP+MLP $\rightarrow$ VQ+Linear) installs the circuit, while a matched-compute MLP control on identical data does not, isolating vector quantization as the source of the pathological signal; the routing pathway that carries it is one that the backbone already provides. Against tuned VCD and DoLA baselines, tuned DoLA wins on binary calibration, but \textbf{only $L_0$ ablation reduces object hallucination in open-ended generation} (CHAIR$_i$ reduces by $31\,\%$ relatively, whereas tuned DoLA and VCD leave it unchanged or worsen it). These results recast object hallucination in unified VQ VLMs as a property of architecture and pretraining, and yield a targeted intervention that mechanism-agnostic decoding cannot replicate.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies an early-layer (L0) attention routing circuit in unified vision-language models (VLMs) that use vector quantization (VQ) codebooks, which causes object hallucination. The authors develop a three-gate diagnostic to identify vulnerable models and show that L0 ablation reduces object hallucination by 31% (CHAIR_i), while decoding-time fixes like VCD and DoLA fail to address this architectural issue.
AI.motivation: Existing decoding-time fixes treat object hallucination in VQ-tokenized VLMs as generic miscalibration without understanding the underlying architectural cause. The authors seek to identify the specific circuit responsible for this pathology.
AI.method: Activation patching across 25 models spanning 8 LLM families; development of a three-gate diagnostic; single-variable architectural swap experiments (LLaVA-1.6 CLIP+MLP → VQ+Linear); comparison with tuned VCD and DoLA baselines
AI.result: L0 ablation reduces object hallucination by 31% relatively (CHAIR_i), while tuned DoLA and VCD leave hallucination unchanged or worsen it. Only L0 ablation reduces hallucination in open-ended generation; tuned DoLA wins on binary calibration but doesn't address the core issue.
AI.conclusion: Object hallucination in unified VQ VLMs is a property of architecture and pretraining, specifically caused by an early-layer attention routing circuit induced by vector quantization. A targeted architectural intervention (L0 ablation) is more effective than mechanism-agnostic decoding methods.

title: EIB-Net: Entropy-Guided Information Bottleneck for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection
summary: The proliferation of photorealistic AI-generated images demands robust detection methods that generalize across diverse generative models. While existing approaches target manipulation-based forgeries with local artifacts, generation-based images (e.g., from diffusion models) lack such traces, posing a fundamental challenge. We observe that generative models prioritize global semantics at the expense of local texture fidelity, making low-texture regions key indicators of synthetic origin. To exploit this, we propose EIB-Net, an Entropy-guided Information Bottleneck Network. EIB-Net introduces a novel Image Entropy (IE) metric to automatically select the most informative (lowest-entropy) patch, then processes it with a Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) to learn compact, generalizable features. Extensive experiments on DIFF, DiffusionForensics, and GenImage benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance: EIB-Net achieves 85.7\% accuracy using only 2\% of training data, outperforming full-image baselines by over 15\%, and maintains robust cross-generator generalization (83.5\% average accuracy on GenImage). Furthermore, our entropy-guided patch selection (EGPL) consistently enhances diverse backbones (CNNs and Transformers), proving its practical value for data-efficient detection.

AI.tldr: EIB-Net is a novel detection method for AI-generated images from diffusion models. It uses image entropy to automatically select informative patches, then applies a Variational Information Bottleneck to learn compact, generalizable features for distinguishing synthetic from real images.
AI.motivation: Existing detection methods target manipulation-based forgeries with local artifacts, but generation-based images from diffusion models lack such traces. The key insight is that generative models sacrifice local texture fidelity for global semantics, making low-texture regions key indicators of synthetic origin.
AI.method: The proposed EIB-Net introduces: 1) Image Entropy (IE) metric to automatically select the most informative (lowest-entropy) patches, and 2) Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) to learn compact, generalizable features. The entropy-guided patch selection (EGPL) can be applied to enhance diverse backbones (CNNs and Transformers).
AI.result: EIB-Net achieves 85.7% accuracy using only 2% of training data, outperforming full-image baselines by over 15%. It maintains robust cross-generator generalization (83.5% average accuracy on GenImage). EGPL consistently enhances diverse backbones.
AI.conclusion: The approach demonstrates that entropy-guided patch selection combined with information bottleneck learning is effective for data-efficient detection of AI-generated images, with strong generalization across different generative models.

title: Seeing Is Not Measuring: Tool-Augmented Metric Spatial Reasoning for Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) describe scenes well but reason poorly about metric 3D structure such as absolute distances, physical sizes, or egocentric directions. We present a modular, predictor agnostic, tool-augmented framework that equips a small VLM (Qwen3.5-4B) with geometric tools: 3D object detection, metric depth estimation, and deterministic solvers for distance, size and bearing. Each object is detected in the camera frame of its own best view, and the tools use that frame's pose to lift every detection into one shared world frame. Moving metric computation out of the model's weights and into explicit solvers yields large gains on three of four ReVSI-Bench tasks: with a strong monocular detector (WildDet3D), absolute distance rises from 0.46 to 0.74 Mean Relative Accuracy (MRA), relative distance from 39.1% to 67.4%, and relative direction from a below-chance 25.9% to 73.4%. Because any detector can be swapped in behind the tool interface, comparing real detectors against ground-truth boxes separates perception error from reasoning error: orchestration costs only 0.03 MRA. Object size is bounded by the detector: the tools are near-exact on groundtruth boxes (0.97) yet the best real detector barely beats the no-tool baseline (0.61 vs. 0.58), because size reads straight off a box extent monocular detectors get wrong. Without a predefined recipe, the model already sequences the tools correctly on its own, matching a scripted pipeline on three of four tasks.

AI.tldr: A framework that augments small Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with geometric tools (3D detection, metric depth, deterministic solvers) to enable metric 3D reasoning about distances, sizes, and directions, achieving significant accuracy gains by moving computation from model weights to explicit solvers.
AI.motivation: Vision-Language Models excel at scene description but struggle with metric 3D structure (absolute distances, physical sizes, egocentric directions). Existing approaches rely on implicit reasoning within model weights, which proves insufficient for precise geometric computations.
AI.method: Modular, predictor-agnostic tool-augmented framework: (1) Each object detected in its camera frame of best view; (2) Tools use that frame's pose to lift detections into a shared world frame; (3) Geometric tools include 3D object detection, metric depth estimation, and deterministic solvers for distance, size, and bearing; (4) Small VLM (Qwen3.5-4B) orchestrates tool usage without predefined recipes.
AI.result: Three of four ReVSI-Bench tasks show large gains: absolute distance MRA 0.46→0.74, relative distance 39.1%→67.4%, relative direction 25.9%→73.4%. Ground-truth boxes achieve near-exact size (0.97), while best real detector barely beats baseline (0.61 vs 0.58). Model sequences tools correctly without scripting, matching scripted pipeline on 3/4 tasks. Orchestration cost is minimal (0.03 MRA).
AI.conclusion: Tool-augmented VLMs can achieve strong metric 3D reasoning by offloading computation to explicit solvers rather than relying on model weights. The modular design separates perception error from reasoning error, with reasoning nearly perfect when using ground-truth boxes. Object size remains bounded by detector performance. The VLM can autonomously sequence tools correctly without predefined recipes.

title: WildHSR: Metric Feed-Forward 4D People-Scene Reconstruction from a 3D Foundation Model
summary: 3D foundation models recover video cameras and geometry in one forward pass, but some of the strongest are up to scale. Joint people-scene reconstruction then requires two missing outputs: metric scale and persistent person identity. We ask whether one up-to-scale foundation representation can support both through lightweight adaptation. Exact metric labels are scarce, but unlabeled in-the-wild video is abundant. We use people in curated web video to initialise the solution: a posed metric body and 2D keypoints give an approximate, closed-form scale pseudo-label. These pseudo-labels pretrain a Scale Readout, which is then fine-tuned together with a lightweight adapter using exact metric supervision from standard real-video training splits. At inference the head predicts metric scale from foundation-model tokens, without the ruler or its teachers. For person identity, we probe the pretrained foundation model alone and find evidence that its intermediate query-key features encode person correspondence across frames. In most evaluated moving-person clips, a mid-layer token prefers that person over the vacated location and other people. A tiny projection reads this correspondence; together with metric pelvis motion and proposal confidence, it drives dustbin-aware Sinkhorn association of per-frame bodies. WildHSR combines both readouts to reconstruct metric cameras, scene and people from monocular video. Each window is predicted feed-forward; analytic association and Sim(3) composition connect windows. On EMDB-2, WildHSR is the first feed-forward method in the published comparison to beat the best optimization-based WA-MPJPE and RTE while leading feed-forward methods on all three world-frame metrics. On RICH, it leads feed-forward people-and-scene methods on WA-MPJPE and W-MPJPE. The complete pipeline runs at 10.1 fps on one GPU.

AI.tldr: WildHSR is a method that adds metric scale and person identity tracking to up-to-scale 3D foundation models for monocular video reconstruction. It uses pseudo-labels from web video to pretrain a Scale Readout, then fine-tunes with exact metric supervision. For identity, it probes intermediate query-key features from the foundation model and uses Sinkhorn association. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on EMDB-2 and RICH benchmarks while running at 10.1 fps.
AI.motivation: 3D foundation models recover video cameras and geometry in one forward pass but are only up-to-scale. Joint people-scene reconstruction requires two missing outputs: metric scale and persistent person identity. The goal is to enable a single up-to-scale foundation representation to support both through lightweight adaptation, without requiring rulers or additional teachers at inference.
AI.method:
1. Scale Readout: Use people in curated web video to generate approximate scale pseudo-labels from posed metric body and 2D keypoints. Pretrain the Scale Readout with these pseudo-labels, then fine-tune with exact metric supervision from standard real-video training splits. At inference, predict metric scale from foundation-model tokens.

2. Person Identity: Probe the pretrained foundation model alone and use intermediate query-key features that encode person correspondence across frames. A tiny projection reads this correspondence, combined with metric pelvis motion and proposal confidence to drive dustbin-aware Sinkhorn association of per-frame bodies.

3. Pipeline: WildHSR combines both readouts to reconstruct metric cameras, scene and people from monocular video. Each window is predicted feed-forward; analytic association and Sim(3) composition connect windows.
AI.result: On EMDB-2, WildHSR is the first feed-forward method to beat the best optimization-based WA-MPJPE and RTE while leading feed-forward methods on all three world-frame metrics. On RICH, it leads feed-forward people-and-scene methods on WA-MPJPE and W-MPJPE. The complete pipeline runs at 10.1 fps on one GPU.
AI.conclusion: Lightweight adaptation of up-to-scale 3D foundation models can recover both metric scale and person identity for joint people-scene reconstruction. The method achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmarks while maintaining real-time performance, demonstrating that intermediate features of foundation models encode valuable correspondence information for tracking.

title: Spectral Amplitude Purification in Distribution Matching for Diffusion Distillation
summary: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) enables high-quality diffusion sampling in only a few steps, but its optimization dynamics remain dominated by coarse, low-frequency signals, delaying the recovery of fine-grained details. We identify a pronounced concentration of spectral amplitudes at low frequencies in the DMD directional error, where dominant low-frequency components overwhelm weaker mid- and high-frequency signals. To address this issue, we propose Spectral Amplitude Purification for Distribution Matching Distillation (SAP-DMD), a plug-and-play approach that adaptively modulates the amplitude spectrum of the DMD directional field. By suppressing the dominant tail of the amplitude spectrum, SAP-DMD reduces low-frequency dominance and promotes more effective recovery of fine structures and textures. Experiments on PixArt-$α$, SD3, and SD3.5 demonstrate that SAP-DMD accelerates training convergence and improves generation quality under both 2-step and 4-step sampling.

AI.tldr: SAP-DMD addresses slow convergence in Distribution Matching Distillation by suppressing dominant low-frequency components in the directional error spectrum, enabling faster recovery of fine-grained details and improved generation quality in few-step diffusion sampling.
AI.motivation: DMD optimization dynamics are dominated by coarse, low-frequency signals, which delays the recovery of fine-grained details. The spectral amplitude of the DMD directional error shows pronounced concentration at low frequencies, where dominant low-frequency components overwhelm weaker mid- and high-frequency signals.
AI.method: SAP-DMD is a plug-and-play approach that adaptively modulates the amplitude spectrum of the DMD directional field. It suppresses the dominant tail of the amplitude spectrum to reduce low-frequency dominance and promote more effective recovery of fine structures and textures.
AI.result: SAP-DMD accelerates training convergence and improves generation quality under both 2-step and 4-step sampling settings. Experiments on PixArt-α, SD3, and SD3.5 demonstrate these improvements.
AI.conclusion: By addressing the spectral imbalance in DMD's optimization dynamics, SAP-DMD successfully enables more effective recovery of fine details while maintaining the efficiency of few-step diffusion sampling.

title: UpDown-SC: Gravity-Canonicalized Dual-Envelope Scan Context for Indoor LiDAR Place Recognition
comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Code and evaluation artifacts: https://github.com/jiejie567/updown-sc
summary: LiDAR place recognition is a key front end for loop closure and global relocalization, yet indoor retrieval remains difficult when attitude or sensor mounting height changes between mapping and query sessions. Scan Context stores the maximum height in each polar cell; indoors, broad ceilings can suppress the lower and mid-level geometry that distinguishes adjacent rooms and corridors. We present UpDown-SC, a training-free polar descriptor that first canonicalizes gravity and then represents two complementary surfaces: the upper envelope of lower/middle structures and the lower envelope of overhead structures. Their physical split is estimated once from a cell-balanced map height distribution and reused by every query. A mask-aware, non-uniform two-channel distance retains discriminative lower-level evidence while limiting sensitivity to its cross-session variation, without treating unobserved cells as zero-height measurements. Conventional Scan Context shortlisting and circular yaw alignment are retained, so retrieved hypotheses directly initialize geometric verification. Experiments across repeated indoor sessions, mounting-height changes, mixed outdoor-to-indoor trajectories, and an outdoor transfer sequence show more reliable first-choice retrieval on the indoor and mounting-height-varied sessions. A paired test finds a significant gain over Scan Context on the in-house sessions. UpDown-SC also gives the best or second-best F1max and AUPR under threshold-based acceptance while retaining a lightweight CPU front end. Continuous replay confirms that the retrieved hypotheses support metric prior-map localization. Code and evaluation artifacts: https://github.com/jiejie567/updown-sc.

AI.tldr: UpDown-SC is a training-free LiDAR place recognition method that addresses indoor retrieval failures caused by attitude or mounting height changes between mapping and query sessions. It uses gravity canonicalization and represents two complementary surfaces (upper envelope of lower structures and lower envelope of overhead structures) to overcome ceiling suppression issues in Scan Context.
AI.motivation: Indoor LiDAR place recognition fails when attitude or sensor mounting height changes between sessions because Scan Context stores maximum height per polar cell, causing broad ceilings to suppress the lower and mid-level geometry that distinguishes adjacent rooms and corridors.
AI.method: UpDown-SC proposes: 1) Gravity canonicalization before descriptor extraction; 2) Two complementary surface representations - upper envelope of lower/middle structures and lower envelope of overhead structures; 3) Physical split estimated once from cell-balanced map height distribution and reused by queries; 4) Mask-aware non-uniform two-channel distance that retains discriminative lower-level evidence while limiting sensitivity to cross-session variation, without treating unobserved cells as zero-height; 5) Retains conventional Scan Context shortlisting and circular yaw alignment for geometric verification initialization.
AI.result: Experiments across repeated indoor sessions, mounting-height changes, mixed outdoor-to-indoor trajectories, and outdoor transfer show more reliable first-choice retrieval on indoor and mounting-height-varied sessions. Paired test shows significant gain over Scan Context on in-house sessions. UpDown-SC achieves best or second-best F1max and AUPR under threshold-based acceptance while retaining lightweight CPU front end. Retrieved hypotheses support metric prior-map localization in continuous replay.
AI.conclusion: UpDown-SC significantly improves indoor LiDAR place recognition under varying sensor configurations without requiring training, making it a practical solution for robust loop closure and global relocalization in indoor environments with height or attitude changes.

title: Less is More: Encoder-only Audio-Visual Segmentation
comment: Submitted to ICASSP 2027. Project page https://ease-avs.notion.site
summary: Audio-Visual Semantic Segmentation (AVSS) aims to identify, segment, and classify sound-emitting objects in video frames. Previous Transformer-based AVSS approaches largely inherit design principles from image segmentation models. Recent studies show that these image segmentation models contain redundant components that contribute little to the segmentation performance. Following this insight, we propose Encoder-only Audio-Visual Segmentation (EASE). EASE runs at up to 365 FPS, 3x faster than prior State-of-the-Art (SotA) AVS models at comparable accuracy, and trains in under 11 GPU-hours. Furthermore, we achieve SotA AVSS performance across different backbones and input resolutions. Our results demonstrate that AVSS can be both simpler and faster, providing a scalable foundation for future research and real-time applications. Code, model weights, and samples are available at https://ease-avs.notion.site

AI.tldr: EASE (Encoder-only Audio-Visual Segmentation) is a simplified, high-performance AVSS model that achieves state-of-the-art results at 365 FPS (3x faster than prior methods) while training in under 11 GPU-hours.
AI.motivation: Previous Transformer-based AVSS approaches inherit design principles from image segmentation models, which contain redundant components that contribute little to segmentation performance. The goal is to demonstrate that AVSS can be both simpler and faster.
AI.method: The paper proposes an Encoder-only architecture (EASE) that removes redundant components found in prior image segmentation-inspired models. The method focuses on streamlining the model while maintaining performance.
AI.result: EASE runs at up to 365 FPS (3x faster than prior SotA), trains in under 11 GPU-hours, and achieves SotA AVSS performance across different backbones and input resolutions.
AI.conclusion: AVSS can be both simpler and faster, providing a scalable foundation for future research and real-time applications.

title: FoCal: Frequency-Oriented Cross-Modal Interaction and Spectral Calibration for Aerial Visible-Infrared Object Detection
summary: In aerial RGB--IR object detection, effectively exploiting complementary information across modalities is critical for robust perception under complex illumination and environmental conditions. Existing multimodal detectors mainly focus on spatial-domain interaction or frequency-specific feature enhancement, while the cross-modal interaction patterns of different frequency components remain insufficiently explored. Moreover, spectral discrepancy itself may contain both useful complementary cues and unreliable modality-specific responses, making indiscriminate frequency fusion suboptimal. To address these issues, we propose FoCal, a frequency-oriented framework for aerial RGB--IR object detection. First, a Frequency-Aware Dual-Domain Calibration (FADC) module is developed to explicitly model frequency-dependent cross-modal interaction. Low-frequency components are collaboratively consolidated into a shared structural consensus, whereas high-frequency components preserve modality-specific information through selective cross-modal exchange. The resulting frequency-aware cues are further transferred to the original feature domain to regulate cross-modal calibration. Second, we introduce a Discrepancy-Guided Spectral Modulation (DGSM) module, which characterizes cross-modal spectral imbalance using confidence-weighted relative amplitude discrepancy and transforms it into a bounded signed gate for adaptive enhancement, preservation, or attenuation of the joint multimodal spectrum. Extensive experiments on DroneVehicle, ESCVehicle, and ATR-UMOD demonstrate the effectiveness of FoCal, yielding $\mathrm{mAP}_{50}$ values of 83.5\%, 54.8\%, and 64.6\%, respectively. Meanwhile, with only 3.0M parameters, FoCal achieves 113.6 FPS while preserving leading detection accuracy, highlighting a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off. Code is available at {https://github.com/universeliang/FoCal.

AI.tldr: FoCal is a frequency-oriented framework for aerial RGB-infrared object detection that addresses limitations in existing multimodal detectors by explicitly modeling frequency-dependent cross-modal interaction. It uses two key modules: FADC for frequency-aware dual-domain calibration and DGSM for discrepancy-guided spectral modulation, achieving state-of-the-art results with only 3.0M parameters and 113.6 FPS.
AI.motivation: The motivation stems from two key issues: (1) Existing multimodal detectors mainly focus on spatial-domain interaction or frequency-specific feature enhancement, while cross-modal interaction patterns of different frequency components remain insufficiently explored; (2) Spectral discrepancy contains both useful complementary cues and unreliable modality-specific responses, making indiscriminate frequency fusion suboptimal. The goal is to develop a framework that can effectively exploit complementary information across RGB and IR modalities under complex illumination and environmental conditions in aerial perception scenarios.
AI.method: The proposed FoCal framework consists of two novel modules: (1) Frequency-Aware Dual-Domain Calibration (FADC) module - explicitly models frequency-dependent cross-modal interaction by consolidating low-frequency components into a shared structural consensus while preserving modality-specific information in high-frequency components through selective cross-modal exchange, then transferring the resulting frequency-aware cues back to the original feature domain; (2) Discrepancy-Guided Spectral Modulation (DGSM) module - characterizes cross-modal spectral imbalance using confidence-weighted relative amplitude discrepancy and transforms it into a bounded signed gate for adaptive enhancement, preservation, or attenuation of the joint multimodal spectrum.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on three aerial vehicle detection datasets demonstrate FoCal's effectiveness: achieving mAP50 of 83.5% on DroneVehicle, 54.8% on ESCVehicle, and 64.6% on ATR-UMOD. Notably, with only 3.0M parameters, FoCal achieves 113.6 FPS, highlighting a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off while preserving leading detection accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The proposed FoCal framework successfully addresses the frequency-oriented challenges in aerial RGB-IR object detection by introducing frequency-aware cross-modal interaction through FADC and discrepancy-guided spectral modulation through DGSM. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks while maintaining real-time inference speed (113.6 FPS) with a lightweight model (3.0M parameters), demonstrating the effectiveness of explicitly modeling frequency-dependent cross-modal interactions and adaptively modulating spectral discrepancy for robust multimodal perception under complex conditions.

title: Recoverable Geographic Location Information in Earth-Observation Embeddings
summary: Earth-observation (EO) foundation models provide reusable embeddings, yet downstream task accuracy does not reveal whether these representations encode geographic information, which may be beneficial for location-aware applications but potentially detrimental when representations invariant to geographic location are desired. We therefore evaluate the geographic coordinate robustness of Tessera v1, Tessera v1.1, and AlphaEarth by testing whether coordinates can be predicted from the embedding representations using 284 quality-verified European solar farms from 2024. We assessed geographic information content information through the association between cosine and geodesic distances and through prediction of projected coordinates in EPSG:3035. Embeddings from all three EO foundation models contain recoverable geographic information. All prediction models significantly outperform training-range uniform random sampling baselines, with AlphaEarth exhibiting the strongest distance association and lowest mean geodesic error. Both Tessera variants also yielded higher geographic distance correlations than the Sentinel-2 controls. These findings motivate geographic information content as an additional criterion for auditing EO foundation models.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates whether Earth-observation foundation models (Tessera v1, Tessera v1.1, and AlphaEarth) encode geographic information in their embeddings by testing coordinate prediction from 284 European solar farms. All models contain recoverable geographic information, with AlphaEarth performing best.
AI.motivation: EO foundation models provide reusable embeddings, but downstream task accuracy doesn't reveal whether representations encode geographic information. This geographic encoding may be beneficial for location-aware applications but detrimental when location-invariant representations are desired. The authors motivation is to audit geographic information content in these models.
AI.method: Using 284 quality-verified European solar farms from 2024, the authors tested whether coordinates can be predicted from embedding representations. They assessed geographic information content through: (1) association between cosine and geodesic distances, and (2) prediction of projected coordinates in EPSG:3035. Performance was compared against uniform random sampling baselines.
AI.result: All three EO foundation model embeddings contain recoverable geographic information. All prediction models significantly outperform training-range uniform random sampling baselines. AlphaEarth exhibits the strongest distance association and lowest mean geodesic error. Both Tessera variants yield higher geographic distance correlations than Sentinel-2 controls.
AI.conclusion: The findings motivate geographic information content as an additional criterion for auditing EO foundation models. This is important for applications where location invariance is desired, as geographic information encoding may be undesirable in certain downstream tasks.

title: Med-AR: Autoregressive Vision-Language Pretraining for Long-Tailed Chest X-Ray Classification and Uncertainty-Aware Evaluation
comment: 80 pages including supplementary material, 28 figures, and 22 tables. Supplementary material is included
summary: Long-tailed chest X-ray classification requires visual representations that capture both common abnormalities and subtle, infrequent findings. We propose Med-AR-8B and Med-AR-2B, two radiology-native autoregressive vision-language models pretrained with structured reports, abnormality-focused text, and region annotations. We evaluate the transfer of their visual encoders to multi-label classification against contrastive, self-supervised, and supervised pretrained encoders, including Med-CLIP, CheXFound, EVA-Base, ARK, and BioViL-T, using a common ML-Decoder classification head. To assess fine-grained recognition, we also construct LLM-expanded, report-derived label sets for MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert. Across PadChest, MIMIC-CXR, and CheXpert, Med-AR-8B outperforms Med-CLIP in mean AUROC and AUPRC for head, medium, and tail findings. On MIMIC-CXR, it increases tail-label mean AUPRC from 0.1033 to 0.1441. Med-AR-2B achieves the strongest discrimination results on PadChest. Across the broader encoder comparison, a Med-AR variant achieves the highest mean AUROC and AUPRC in every reported prevalence group on each public dataset. Both Med-AR variants also achieve lower excess area under the risk-coverage curve than Med-CLIP on all three public datasets, indicating improved selective-prediction performance under the evaluated protocol. Internal results are metric-dependent, with Med-CLIP retaining advantages in overall and tail AUPRC and in selective prediction. These findings establish Med-AR as a strong pretraining recipe for long-tailed chest X-ray classification on the evaluated public benchmarks and demonstrate the value of assessing discrimination and selective prediction together.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Med-AR-8B and Med-AR-2B, radiology-native autoregressive vision-language models pretrained with structured reports, abnormality-focused text, and region annotations for long-tailed chest X-ray classification. These models aim to capture both common abnormalities and subtle, infrequent findings.
AI.motivation: Long-tailed chest X-ray classification requires visual representations that capture both common abnormalities (head) and subtle, infrequent findings (tail). Existing models may not adequately represent rare conditions, necessitating a new pretraining approach.
AI.method: The authors develop Med-AR-8B and Med-AR-2B, radiology-native autoregressive vision-language models pretrained with structured reports, abnormality-focused text, and region annotations. They evaluate transfer of visual encoders to multi-label classification using ML-Decoder head, comparing against Med-CLIP, CheXFound, EVA-Base, ARK, and BioViL-T. They also construct LLM-expanded, report-derived label sets for MIMIC-CXR and CheXpert to assess fine-grained recognition.
AI.result: Med-AR-8B outperforms Med-CLIP in mean AUROC and AUPRC for head, medium, and tail findings across PadChest, MIMIC-CXR, and CheXpert. On MIMIC-CXR, tail-label mean AUPRC increased from 0.1033 to 0.1441. Med-AR-2B achieves best discrimination on PadChest. Med-AR variants achieve highest mean AUROC and AUPRC in every prevalence group on each public dataset. They also show lower excess area under risk-coverage curve than Med-CLIP, indicating improved selective-prediction performance.
AI.conclusion: Med-AR represents a strong pretraining recipe for long-tailed chest X-ray classification on public benchmarks. Assessing discrimination and selective prediction together provides valuable insights into model performance across different prevalence groups.

title: An Automated Georeferencing Technique for Multi-Temporal Stope Point Clouds for Downstream Geotechnical Analysis
summary: The increasing use of UAV laser scanning in underground mines has enabled frequent acquisition of 3D point clouds from challenging environments such as stopes, generating large volumes of multi-temporal spatial data throughout successive excavation stages. However, in GNSS-denied underground environments, independently acquired stope point clouds are generated within local scanner reference frames and require registration and georeferencing before integration with mine reference data for downstream geotechnical analysis, monitoring, and mine planning. This process is commonly performed manually by aligning individual stope scans with mine reference drives, making repeated georeferencing time-consuming and potentially limiting the utilisation of routinely acquired data. This study proposes the 3D Tag-based Automated Registration and Georeferencing Technique (3D-TARGeT), an automated framework using low-cost, generic, non-unique rectangular tags to establish spatial correspondence between stope point clouds and the mine reference coordinate system. The framework combines automated tag identification, geometric tag matching, and rigid transformation estimation. It was evaluated as a proof of concept using four multi-temporal point-cloud scans of an underground mine stope, with the proposed tags simulated under representative scanning conditions. 3D-TARGeT achieved consistent centimetre-level georeferencing accuracy, with median cloud-to-cloud distance and root mean square error below 0.03 m across all scans, while substantially outperforming widely used automatic point-cloud registration techniques. Overall, 3D-TARGeT provides an accurate and robust approach for automating stope point-cloud georeferencing, reducing reliance on manual alignment and facilitating multi-temporal datasets for downstream geological and geotechnical applications.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes 3D-TARGeT, an automated framework for registering and georeferencing UAV laser scanning point clouds in underground mine stopes using low-cost rectangular tags, achieving consistent centimeter-level accuracy (median distance and RMSE below 0.03 m) and outperforming existing automatic registration techniques.
AI.motivation: UAV laser scanning enables frequent 3D point cloud acquisition in underground mines, but GNSS-denied environments require manual registration and georeferencing of stope point clouds to mine reference coordinates, which is time-consuming and limits the utilization of routinely acquired data.
AI.method: The 3D-TARGeT framework combines automated tag identification, geometric tag matching, and rigid transformation estimation using low-cost, generic, non-unique rectangular tags to establish spatial correspondence between stope point clouds and the mine reference coordinate system. It was evaluated using four multi-temporal point-cloud scans of an underground mine stope with simulated tags under representative scanning conditions.
AI.result: 3D-TARGeT achieved consistent centimeter-level georeferencing accuracy, with median cloud-to-cloud distance and root mean square error below 0.03 m across all scans, while substantially outperforming widely used automatic point-cloud registration techniques.
AI.conclusion: 3D-TARGeT provides an accurate and robust approach for automating stope point-cloud georeferencing, reducing reliance on manual alignment and facilitating multi-temporal datasets for downstream geological and geotechnical applications.

title: ImCorr: Sub-pixel Semantic Correspondence via Implicit Feature Decoding
summary: The strong performance that modern semantic correspondence methods achieve at standard thresholds plateaus sharply at fine-grained thresholds. We argue that this plateau stems not from the representational capacity of backbone features, but from a grid-tied readout. Patch-based vision transformers tokenize images onto discrete grids, introducing two forms of quantization error: querying nearest patch features instead of exact keypoints on the source side, and the absence of grid features representing precise ground-truth locations on the target side. We quantify this quantization ceiling across all 499,188 keypoints in SPair-71k: under the standard 448x448, patch-14 setting, 84.9% of ground-truth keypoints have no grid feature representing their precise location at PCK@0.01. This is a structural limitation at the representation level, independent of the matching strategy. We address this with ImCorr: Sub-pixel Semantic Correspondence via Implicit Feature Decoding, which formulates correspondence estimation over a continuous feature field queryable at arbitrary continuous coordinates. A FiLM-conditioned decoder is trained to embed sub-pixel positional information into the feature field. Querying the field directly at exact keypoint coordinates theoretically eliminates representation-level quantization error on the source side, while decoding onto a grid denser than the backbone grid substantially reduces quantization error on the target side. On SPair-71k and AP-10K (intra-species, cross-species, and cross-family), ImCorr improves performance at fine-grained thresholds (PCK@0.01-0.05), achieving a 6.2 percentage point gain over the prior state of the art at PCK@0.01 on SPair-71k. These results demonstrate that representational continuity is an effective solution for precise semantic correspondence. Code is available at https://github.com/YusungChoi/ImCorr.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses a fundamental limitation in semantic correspondence: patch-based vision transformers introduce quantization errors that prevent accurate keypoint matching at fine-grained thresholds. The proposed ImCorr method uses implicit feature decoding to enable continuous coordinate querying, eliminating representation-level quantization error.
AI.motivation: The authors observed that modern semantic correspondence methods achieve strong performance at standard thresholds but plateau sharply at fine-grained thresholds (PCK@0.01-0.05). They identified the root cause as grid-tied readout in patch-based vision transformers, which introduces two forms of quantization error: (1) querying nearest patch features instead of exact keypoints on the source side, and (2) absence of grid features representing precise ground-truth locations on the target side. Quantification on SPair-71k showed 84.9% of ground-truth keypoints have no grid feature representing their precise location at PCK@0.01.
AI.method: The authors propose ImCorr (Implicit Correspondence), which formulates correspondence estimation over a continuous feature field queryable at arbitrary continuous coordinates. Key components include: (1) A FiLM-conditioned decoder trained to embed sub-pixel positional information into the feature field, (2) Direct field querying at exact keypoint coordinates to eliminate source-side quantization error, and (3) Decoding onto a denser grid than the backbone grid to reduce target-side quantization error.
AI.result: ImCorr achieves significant improvements at fine-grained thresholds on SPair-71k and AP-10K (covering intra-species, cross-species, and cross-family scenarios). The method achieves a 6.2 percentage point gain over the prior state of the art at PCK@0.01 on SPair-71k, demonstrating that representational continuity is an effective solution for precise semantic correspondence.
AI.conclusion: The paper demonstrates that quantization error from patch-based vision transformers is a structural limitation at the representation level, independent of the matching strategy. ImCorr's implicit feature decoding approach successfully addresses this limitation by enabling continuous coordinate querying, establishing representational continuity as an effective solution for precise semantic correspondence. The code is available at https://github.com/YusungChoi/ImCorr.

title: FounRef: Robust, Structure-Preserving, and Fast Metric Refinement of Frozen Monocular Foundation Priors with Sparse Anchors
summary: Dense metric depth from cameras is essential to real-world 3D applications, yet achieving accuracy, faithful surface geometry, and fast inference simultaneously remains challenging. Monocular foundation models provide rich, transferable geometric priors but lack reliable metric scale, while depth-completion networks recover metric depth at the cost of geometric fidelity, cross-domain robustness, or speed. We present FounRef, a training-free method that aligns a frozen monocular foundation prior with sparse metric anchors to produce dense metric depth. FounRef is modular by design: its depth prior, anchor source, and refinement solver can each be replaced independently. We instantiate FounRef with MoGe-2 and LiDAR anchors. FounRef validates each anchor against the prior's dense depth prediction, rejecting inconsistencies caused by cross-sensor misalignment that geometry-only filters cannot detect. It then applies global and local metric corrections through a structure-preserving solver, retaining the prior's fine-grained geometry. FounRef requires no task-specific training and operates out of the box across unfamiliar cameras and scenes. On out-of-domain data, it delivers up to 24% lower depth error, 92% lower surface-normal noise, and almost 15x faster inference than DMD3C, a state-of-the-art depth-completion network. By decoupling metric alignment from geometry prediction, FounRef provides an accurate, geometrically faithful, and efficient approach to dense metric depth that can directly benefit from future advances in foundation models and metric sensors.

AI.tldr: FounRef is a training-free method that aligns a frozen monocular foundation model prior with sparse LiDAR anchors to produce dense metric depth. It validates anchors against the prior's prediction to reject inconsistencies, then applies global and local metric corrections through a structure-preserving solver.
AI.motivation: Dense metric depth from cameras is essential for 3D applications, but achieving accuracy, faithful surface geometry, and fast inference simultaneously remains challenging. Monocular foundation models lack reliable metric scale, while depth-completion networks sacrifice geometric fidelity, cross-domain robustness, or speed.
AI.method: FounRef uses a modular design with three replaceable components: depth prior, anchor source, and refinement solver. It instantiates with MoGe-2 prior and LiDAR anchors. The method validates each anchor against the prior's dense depth prediction to reject inconsistencies caused by cross-sensor misalignment. It then applies global and local metric corrections through a structure-preserving solver while retaining fine-grained geometry.
AI.result: On out-of-domain data, FounRef delivers up to 24% lower depth error, 92% lower surface-normal noise, and almost 15x faster inference than DMD3C (state-of-the-art depth-completion network).
AI.conclusion: FounRef provides an accurate, geometrically faithful, and efficient approach to dense metric depth by decoupling metric alignment from geometry prediction. It requires no task-specific training, operates out-of-the-box across unfamiliar cameras and scenes, and can directly benefit from future advances in foundation models and metric sensors.

title: ComplexSync: High-Fidelity and Real-Time Lip Sync in Complex Scenarios
summary: Lip synchronization aims to generate visual lip dynamics that align precisely with speech audio. Despite the high generation quality of diffusion models, they often struggle in complex scenarios and suffer from prohibitive inference latency, limiting real-world deployment. We present ComplexSync, a unified diffusion-based framework that enables real-time, high-fidelity lip sync under complex conditions. First, we introduce a dual-stream joint training strategy to mitigate information leakage from reference frames while preserving natural dynamics. Second, we develop a distillation-based acceleration scheme for single-step denoising, achieving a throughput of over 70 FPS. Third, we propose a relational alignment loss that leverages structural priors from Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) to enhance robustness against complex scene factors. Furthermore, we present the first benchmark specifically designed for complex lip synchronization, comprising over 200 challenging video sequences and specialized metrics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ComplexSync achieves state-of-the-art performance across both standard and complex scenarios while enabling real-time inference.

AI.tldr: ComplexSync is a real-time diffusion-based lip synchronization framework that addresses challenges in complex scenarios and high latency. It introduces a dual-stream training strategy, distillation-based acceleration achieving 70+ FPS, and a relational alignment loss using Vision Foundation Models. The paper also presents the first benchmark for complex lip synchronization with 200+ challenging videos.
AI.motivation: Lip synchronization using diffusion models faces two critical limitations: (1) poor performance in complex scenarios, and (2) prohibitive inference latency that prevents real-world deployment.
AI.method: Three technical contributions: (1) Dual-stream joint training strategy to mitigate information leakage from reference frames while preserving natural dynamics; (2) Distillation-based acceleration scheme for single-step denoising; (3) Relational alignment loss leveraging structural priors from Vision Foundation Models (VFMs). Additionally, a new benchmark with 200+ challenging video sequences and specialized metrics was introduced.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across both standard and complex scenarios while enabling real-time inference at over 70 FPS throughput.
AI.conclusion: ComplexSync successfully enables real-time, high-fidelity lip synchronization under complex conditions through innovative training, acceleration, and loss design, along with a dedicated benchmark for evaluation.

title: SARFusion: Scene-Aware Routing Fusion for Robust Camera-LiDAR 3D Object Detection
summary: Camera-LiDAR fusion has become a prevailing paradigm for 3D object detection in autonomous driving. However, existing fusion detectors often establish strong inter-modality dependencies by decoding object queries from tightly coupled multimodal representations. Under corrupted driving conditions, such dependencies make the detector vulnerable to unreliable modalities, where degraded observations may interfere with reliable modality-specific evidence and lead to suboptimal predictions. Moreover, modality reliability can vary across both global driving scenes and individual object queries, requiring adaptive fusion decisions at a finer granularity. To bridge this gap, we reformulate robust camera-LiDAR fusion as a scene-aware branch routing problem and propose SARFusion, a robust 3D object detector. Instead of producing detections from a single fused representation, SARFusion decouples object-query decoding into three parallel reasoning branches: a camera branch, a LiDAR branch, and a camera-LiDAR fusion branch. Guided by a Scene Reliability Prior estimated from the global driving context, SARFusion further incorporates object-level evidence to route each query to the most suitable branch. This query-wise routing strategy alleviates harmful cross-modal interference while preserving the benefits of multimodal fusion when complementary cues are trustworthy. On the nuScenes test set, SARFusion achieves strong performance with 72.5 mAP and 74.4 NDS. Extensive analyses demonstrate its robustness under challenging conditions, including sensor corruptions and environmental changes.

AI.tldr: SARFusion addresses robust 3D object detection in autonomous driving by reformulating camera-LiDAR fusion as a scene-aware branch routing problem. It uses three parallel reasoning branches (camera, LiDAR, fusion) with query-wise routing guided by a Scene Reliability Prior to adaptively select the most reliable modality for each object query.
AI.motivation: Existing fusion detectors establish strong inter-modality dependencies that make them vulnerable to unreliable modalities under corrupted driving conditions. Degraded observations from one modality can interfere with reliable modality-specific evidence. Additionally, modality reliability varies across both global driving scenes and individual object queries, requiring adaptive fusion at finer granularity.
AI.method: SARFusion decouples object-query decoding into three parallel reasoning branches: camera branch, LiDAR branch, and camera-LiDAR fusion branch. A Scene Reliability Prior is estimated from global driving context to guide object-level evidence for routing each query to the most suitable branch. This query-wise routing strategy alleviates harmful cross-modal interference while preserving multimodal fusion benefits when complementary cues are trustworthy.
AI.result: On nuScenes test set, SARFusion achieves 72.5 mAP and 74.4 NDS. Extensive analyses demonstrate robustness under challenging conditions including sensor corruptions and environmental changes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed scene-aware branch routing approach effectively addresses vulnerability to unreliable modalities in camera-LiDAR fusion. By enabling adaptive selection between modality-specific and fused representations at the query level, SARFusion achieves strong detection performance while maintaining robustness across diverse and challenging driving conditions.

title: TOLA: Text-aware One-Step Latent Adaptation for Diffusion-based Text Image Super-Resolution
summary: Text image super-resolution (TSR) aims to recover visually faithful and readable text under unknown degradations. Existing diffusion-based methods typically rely on multi-step prediction of either the high-resolution image or its text prior, resulting in prohibitive computational cost and inference latency. More critically, an erroneous text prior may be repeatedly injected into the denoising process, causing image and text predictions to reinforce each other and progressively amplify an early recognition error into a sharp yet semantically incorrect character. To address these limitations, we propose TOLA, a Text-aware One-step Latent Adaptation framework without iterative image-text diffusion. TOLA consists of two key modules. First, a confidence-weighted text conditioning module constructs the semantic condition only once and suppresses unreliable OCR predictions before they contaminate image reconstruction. Second, a lightweight latent residual correction module explicitly estimates and corrects the structured residual errors to recover missing or distorted stroke details. Extensive experiments demonstrate our state-of-the-art performance across all evaluation metrics on both CTR-TSR-Test ($\times 4$) and RealCE-200 benchmarks. It is worth noting that our TOLA consistently surpasses existing diffusion-based TSR methods by at least 2.72 dB in PSNR on CTR-TSR-Test.

AI.tldr: TOLA is a novel text image super-resolution framework that achieves state-of-the-art performance through a one-step latent adaptation approach, avoiding the computational cost and error amplification issues of iterative diffusion methods. It uses confidence-weighted text conditioning to suppress unreliable OCR predictions and latent residual correction to recover stroke details, outperforming existing methods by at least 2.72 dB in PSNR.
AI.motivation: Text image super-resolution (TSR) aims to recover visually faithful and readable text under unknown degradations. Existing diffusion-based methods suffer from two critical limitations: 1) Multi-step prediction leads to prohibitive computational cost and inference latency; 2) Erroneous text prior may be repeatedly injected into the denoising process, causing image and text predictions to reinforce each other and progressively amplify early recognition errors into semantically incorrect characters.
AI.method: TOLA (Text-aware One-step Latent Adaptation) framework without iterative image-text diffusion. It consists of two key modules: 1) Confidence-weighted text conditioning module - constructs semantic condition only once and suppresses unreliable OCR predictions before they contaminate image reconstruction; 2) Lightweight latent residual correction module - explicitly estimates and corrects structured residual errors to recover missing or distorted stroke details.
AI.result: State-of-the-art performance across all evaluation metrics on both CTR-TSR-Test (×4) and RealCE-200 benchmarks. TOLA consistently surpasses existing diffusion-based TSR methods by at least 2.72 dB in PSNR on CTR-TSR-Test.
AI.conclusion: The proposed TOLA effectively addresses the limitations of existing diffusion-based TSR methods by eliminating iterative image-text diffusion through a one-step latent adaptation approach. The confidence-weighted text conditioning module prevents unreliable OCR predictions from contaminating image reconstruction, while the latent residual correction module recovers missing stroke details. This results in superior performance in terms of both visual quality and computational efficiency.

title: IronViT: Toward Efficient Generalist Visual Representation Learning
summary: A generalist vision encoder must capture semantic, spatial, language-aligned, and action-relevant cues within a unified representation, yet softmax attention underlying today's most capable visual backbones becomes prohibitively expensive at high resolution. A natural attempt to address both challenges is to distill multiple specialist teachers directly into an efficient architecture. We find that directly coupling these objectives degrades representation quality, as the student must simultaneously reconcile heterogeneous capabilities and adapt them to a different token-mixing architecture. We introduce IronViT, built on a simple principle: consolidate capabilities before constraining computation. IronViT first distills complementary specialists into a softmax attention capability bridge, then progressively transfers the consolidated representation to a hybrid softmax-linear attention encoder. A purpose-built data pipeline further curates the distillation corpus for higher information density and broader domain coverage. Across recognition, retrieval, dense prediction, multimodal understanding, and robotic learning, IronViT is competitive with leading specialist and generalist vision encoders. The softmax bridge achieves the strongest aggregate performance in multimodal understanding and robotic learning among the evaluated backbones, while the hybrid encoder retains broad transfer performance with an efficiency advantage that grows with input resolution. Together, these results show that consolidating capabilities before architectural conversion can yield a generalist visual encoder without inheriting the prohibitive high-resolution cost of conventional softmax attention.

AI.tldr: IronViT is a generalist vision encoder that consolidates capabilities from multiple specialist teachers via a softmax attention "bridge" before transferring to a more efficient hybrid softmax-linear attention encoder, achieving competitive performance across recognition, retrieval, dense prediction, multimodal understanding, and robotic learning tasks without the high-resolution cost of conventional softmax attention.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to create a generalist vision encoder that captures semantic, spatial, language-aligned, and action-relevant cues while addressing the prohibitive computational cost of softmax attention at high resolution. Direct distillation of multiple specialists into an efficient architecture degrades representation quality due to the student's need to simultaneously reconcile heterogeneous capabilities and adapt to a different token-mixing architecture.
AI.method: IronViT employs a two-stage approach: (1) First distill complementary specialist teachers into a softmax attention "capability bridge" to consolidate diverse capabilities, then (2) progressively transfer the consolidated representation to a hybrid softmax-linear attention encoder. Additionally, a purpose-built data pipeline curates the distillation corpus for higher information density and broader domain coverage.
AI.result: IronViT achieves competitive performance with leading specialist and generalist vision encoders across recognition, retrieval, dense prediction, multimodal understanding, and robotic learning tasks. The softmax bridge achieves the strongest aggregate performance in multimodal understanding and robotic learning among evaluated backbones, while the hybrid encoder retains broad transfer performance with an efficiency advantage that grows with input resolution.
AI.conclusion: Consolidating capabilities before architectural conversion can yield a generalist visual encoder without inheriting the prohibitive high-resolution cost of conventional softmax attention. This approach successfully balances broad capability coverage with computational efficiency.

title: Deep learning of longitudinal visual fields predicts glaucoma progression rate and identifies fast progressors
summary: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness, and timely identification of fast progressors is essential to prevent disability. Current practice estimates progression by ordinary least-squares regression of mean deviation (MD) on time, requiring 6--10 visual field (VF) tests over several years to obtain a reliable slope. We present GLAM (Glaucoma Longitudinal Analysis Model), a deep learning framework that ingests longitudinal Humphrey 24-2 total deviation sequences with five clinical features and predicts MD and visual field index progression rates using attention-based fusion and aleatoric uncertainty. On the open-access University of Washington Humphrey Visual Field dataset (4,276 patient-eyes), GLAM achieved an MD-rate mean absolute error of 0.139 dB yr$^{-1}$ ($R^2 = 0.927$; 73.5% reduction over a ridge baseline) and an AUC of 0.990 for fast-progressor detection. VF-only deep learning can match multimodal pipelines for progression prognostication using routinely collected perimetry alone.

AI.tldr: GLAM is a deep learning framework that predicts glaucoma progression rates from visual field sequences and clinical features, achieving superior accuracy (0.139 dB/yr MAE, R²=0.927) and fast-progressor detection (AUC=0.990) compared to traditional regression methods.
AI.motivation: Current glaucoma progression estimation requires 6-10 visual field tests over several years using ordinary least-squares regression, which is slow and inefficient. There is a need for faster, more accurate identification of fast progressors to prevent irreversible blindness.
AI.method: Deep learning framework using attention-based fusion and aleatoric uncertainty, ingesting longitudinal Humphrey 24-2 total deviation sequences with five clinical features to predict MD and VFI progression rates.
AI.result: MD-rate MAE of 0.139 dB/yr (R²=0.927), representing a 73.5% reduction over ridge regression baseline. Fast-progressor detection AUC of 0.990. Notably, VF-only deep learning matched multimodal pipelines.
AI.conclusion: Visual field-only deep learning can match multimodal pipelines for glaucoma progression prognostication using routinely collected perimetry alone, enabling earlier identification of fast progressors with fewer tests.

title: PHOSA: Photorealistic 3D Sign Avatar Modeling and Benchmark
summary: In this work, we focus on photorealistic sign avatar modeling, which is crucial for effective communication with the Deaf community and is characterized by complex hand gestures and nuanced facial expressions. To this end, we introduce MVSign, the first multi-view Chinese sign language dataset co-designed with Deaf experts, featuring diverse gestures and rich annotations. For precise SMPL-X annotation, we develop a hybrid fitting pipeline that produces accurate body, hand, and facial parameters and can also be applied to the monocular setting. Building on MVSign, we propose a decoupled sign avatar representation that isolates body, head, and hand components to capture complex articulations, together with a motion-aware sampling strategy to handle motion blur and balance gesture diversity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves high-fidelity visual results on MVSign, particularly in detailed hand and facial regions, and generalizes well to in-the-wild monocular sign language videos. Project page: https://naaapi.github.io/PHOSA.

AI.tldr: MVSign is the first multi-view Chinese sign language dataset co-designed with Deaf experts, enabling photorealistic sign avatar modeling with complex hand gestures and facial expressions. The method uses a hybrid fitting pipeline for SMPL-X annotation and proposes a decoupled avatar representation with motion-aware sampling.
AI.motivation: Effective communication with the Deaf community requires photorealistic sign avatar modeling that can capture complex hand gestures and nuanced facial expressions, which is challenging due to the complexity of sign language movements.
AI.method: 1) MVSign dataset: first multi-view Chinese sign language dataset with diverse gestures and rich annotations, co-designed with Deaf experts. 2) Hybrid fitting pipeline: produces accurate SMPL-X parameters for body, hand, and facial regions, applicable to both multi-view and monocular settings. 3) Decoupled sign avatar representation: isolates body, head, and hand components to capture complex articulations. 4) Motion-aware sampling strategy: handles motion blur and balances gesture diversity.
AI.result: The method achieves high-fidelity visual results on MVSign, particularly in detailed hand and facial regions, and generalizes well to in-the-wild monocular sign language videos.
AI.conclusion: The proposed MVSign dataset and decoupled representation with motion-aware sampling enable photorealistic sign avatar modeling with accurate hand and facial details, demonstrating good generalization to monocular in-the-wild scenarios.

title: Hyperbolic Multimodal Continual Learning: A Closest-Admissible Solution
summary: Existing continual-learning methods protect parameters, replayed examples, or Euclidean feature subspaces. When applied to hyperbolic multimodal models, they do not explicitly preserve the Lorentz geometry that jointly encodes within-modality similarity, cross-modal correspondence, and semantic hierarchy; sequential updates can therefore retain task scores while still distorting previously learned relations. We address this gap with Hyperbolic Multimodal Continual Learning (HMCL). We show that preserving the old multimodal geometry amounts to restricting all modalities to one shared hyperbolic isometry, which induces a family of admissible first-order parameter changes. We formulate a joint closest-admissible (CA) correction that retains the shared rotation best matching the candidate modal updates; its minimal-rotation (MR) special case fixes this rotation to zero. Both variants correct the displacement realized by AdamW, and task anchoring bounds within-task accumulation while preserving learning freedom. Across a unified 16-task classification-retrieval stream with three hyperbolic backbones, HMCL improves final performance and backward transfer over sequential fine-tuning and four continual-learning baselines; HMCL-CA gives the highest Overall score on every backbone. A modality-extended stream confirms the retrieval gains. Representation analyses find 81.2 to 95.5 percent less radial, angular, cross-modal, and paired-distance drift; ImageNet-WordNet results show better semantic ancestry and radial hierarchy.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses catastrophic forgetting in hyperbolic multimodal models by proposing Hyperbolic Multimodal Continual Learning (HMCL), which preserves the Lorentz geometry that encodes within-modality similarity, cross-modal correspondence, and semantic hierarchy. The method restricts all modalities to one shared hyperbolic isometry and applies joint closest-admissible (CA) or minimal-rotation (MR) corrections to AdamW updates.
AI.motivation: Existing continual-learning methods protect parameters, replayed examples, or Euclidean feature subspaces but fail to preserve Lorentz geometry in hyperbolic multimodal models. This causes sequential updates to distort previously learned relations even when task scores are retained.
AI.method: HMCL preserves old multimodal geometry by restricting all modalities to one shared hyperbolic isometry, inducing admissible first-order parameter changes. Two variants are proposed: (1) CA (closest-admissible) correction retains the shared rotation best matching candidate modal updates; (2) MR (minimal-rotation) special case fixes rotation to zero. Both correct AdamW displacement with task anchoring to bound within-task accumulation while preserving learning freedom.
AI.result: Across a unified 16-task classification-retrieval stream with three hyperbolic backbones, HMCL improves final performance and backward transfer over sequential fine-tuning and four continual-learning baselines. HMCL-CA achieves the highest Overall score on every backbone. Modality-extended stream confirms retrieval gains. Representation analyses show 81.2 to 95.5 percent less radial, angular, cross-modal, and paired-distance drift. ImageNet-WordNet results demonstrate better semantic ancestry and radial hierarchy.
AI.conclusion: HMCL successfully preserves hyperbolic multimodal geometry during continual learning, significantly reducing geometric distortion while maintaining or improving task performance. The CA variant consistently outperforms all baselines across all tested backbones.

title: A Study of the Limits of Collaborative DCT-Based Image Denoising via Interpretable Neural Networks
comment: Preprint submitted to Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision (JMIV). 17 pages, 11 figures. Supported by MCIN/AEI/10.13039/501100011033 under grant PID2021-125711OB-I00, and by the Spanish Ministry of Universities under grant FPU24/02805
summary: Image denoising remains a fundamental problem in image restoration, with applications in photography, biomedical, and scientific imaging. Modern deep neural networks achieve strong performance by learning powerful image priors, but often rely on large black-box models with limited interpretability. In contrast, DCT-based sliding-window and collaborative filtering methods such as BM3D offer clear algorithmic structure, but depend on handcrafted and non-differentiable operations. This work studies how far such structured collaborative filtering principles can be pushed when reformulated as trainable models. We introduce DeepBM3D, a compact fully differentiable architecture that combines non-local patch grouping, DCT-domain filtering, and multi-stage refinement within a BM3D-inspired pipeline. Lightweight convolutional feature extractors guide patch grouping, while filtering is performed through learned Wiener weights in the DCT domain. Experiments show that DeepBM3D improves over classical and hybrid baselines, remains competitive with FFDNet at low and moderate noise levels, and performs particularly well on repetitive textures.

AI.tldr: DeepBM3D is a compact fully differentiable image denoising architecture that combines BM3D's collaborative filtering principles with learnable components, using convolutional feature extractors for patch grouping and learned Wiener weights in DCT domain for filtering.
AI.motivation: Bridge the gap between interpretable but non-differentiable traditional methods (like BM3D) and powerful but black-box deep learning approaches. The goal is to create a trainable model that maintains clear algorithmic structure while achieving competitive denoising performance.
AI.method: DeepBM3D combines: (1) lightweight convolutional feature extractors for patch grouping guidance, (2) DCT-domain filtering with learned Wiener weights, and (3) multi-stage refinement - all within a BM3D-inspired pipeline that is fully differentiable.
AI.result: DeepBM3D improves over classical and hybrid baselines, remains competitive with FFDNet at low/moderate noise levels, and performs particularly well on repetitive textures.
AI.conclusion: Structured collaborative filtering principles from BM3D can be effectively reformulated as trainable models, achieving a good balance between interpretability and performance. The approach demonstrates the potential of combining domain knowledge with deep learning in image restoration.

title: SEE Challenge 2026: Event-Guided Brightness Adjustment Across a Broad Illumination Range
comment: This report has been accepted for publication at an ECCV 2026 Workshop
summary: Event cameras provide a high dynamic range and preserve brightness-change cues in lighting conditions where conventional RGB frames may be noisy or saturated. To benchmark event-guided restoration across a broad illumination range, we organized the SEE Challenge 2026 with the Event-Based Multimodal Vision Workshop at ECCV 2026. The task conditions restoration on one or more RGB frames, synchronized events, and a scalar target-brightness statistic provided by the organizers. It uses SEE-600K, which contains 610,126 image-event observations from 202 real-world scenes spanning low-light, normal-light, and high-light conditions with illumination variations of up to 1,000$\times$. The challenge follows an open-system protocol: participants may use different temporal contexts, architectures, pretrained weights, test-time augmentation, and post-processing strategies. PSNR determines the ranking, and SSIM is reported as a secondary metric. Around 70 teams registered interest and 15 valid CodaBench submissions were received. Six distinct teams completed organizer-side identity and technical verification, provided method descriptions, checkpoints, inference code, and instructions, and are included in the verified open-system ranking reported here. Beyond the ranking, this report analyzes exposure subsets, semantically distinct test cases, a shared failure pattern, system design choices, and inference strategies. The top systems obtain closely spaced average scores, while the best-performing method varies across cases and metrics; under severe underexposure, all verified systems retain visible local errors.

AI.tldr: The SEE Challenge 2026 benchmarks event-guided image restoration using the SEE-600K dataset with 610K observations across 202 scenes and illumination variations up to 1,000×. Participants used RGB frames, synchronized events, and target brightness statistics. PSNR ranked submissions, with 6 teams completing verification out of 15 valid submissions.
AI.motivation: Event cameras offer high dynamic range and preserve brightness-change cues in challenging lighting conditions where conventional RGB frames become noisy or saturated. The challenge aims to benchmark event-guided restoration across a broad illumination range, addressing limitations of traditional vision systems in variable lighting.
AI.method: The challenge uses an open-system protocol allowing participants flexibility in temporal contexts, architectures, pretrained weights, test-time augmentation, and post-processing strategies. Input includes one or more RGB frames, synchronized events, and a scalar target-brightness statistic. The SEE-600K dataset contains 610,126 image-event observations from 202 real-world scenes spanning low-light, normal-light, and high-light conditions.

Top systems achieved closely spaced average scores, with the best-performing method varying across cases and metrics. Under severe underexposure, all verified systems retained visible local errors.
